definition_zh: 干预；介入；调停
definition_en: the act of becoming involved in a situation from outside, especially to change or stop it
core_image: 会议桌旁原本两方对坐，忽然多出一把椅子放在正中
scene: 两国谈判陷入僵局，第三方派出代表带着折中方案来到桌边。 Early medical intervention saved the patient's hand.
sceneCN: 这里 intervention 是「干预、介入」（第 1 个义项：外部力量插手），句意为早期医疗介入保住了病人的手。画面里的物件：折中方案、多出的一把椅子、病历。

derivatives.zh: 去后缀构成，义为「干预；介入」
加 -ist 构成，义为「干预主义者」
加 -al 构成，义为「介入性的」

senses.title: An act from outside
senses.definition: action taken by a person, group, or state to alter a situation it is not directly part of
senses.definitionCN: 由个人、团体或国家对本不直接属于自己的一方局面采取的、意在改变它的行动
senses.example: The court's intervention ended the strike.
senses.exampleCN: 法院的介入结束了罢工。
senses.why: Latin interventio named the act of coming in between, and the noun keeps it as a thing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 interventio 指「来到中间」这个动作，名词把它变成一件事。

senses.title: Steps taken to help
senses.definition: professional action taken to improve a person's health, education, or safety
senses.definitionCN: 为改善某人的健康、教育或安全而采取的专业行动
senses.example: Early intervention helps children with hearing problems.
senses.exampleCN: 早期介入对听力有问题的孩子很有帮助。
senses.why: Medicine and teaching softened the word: intervention can be care rather than force.
senses.whyCN: 医学与教育让这个词变软：介入不必是强制，也可以是照护。

senses.title: Stopping a fight
senses.definition: the act of stepping into a conflict in order to separate the parties or end it
senses.definitionCN: 进入冲突以分开双方或结束冲突的行为
senses.example: His intervention stopped the quarrel before anyone was hurt.
senses.exampleCN: 他的介入让争吵在人受伤前就停了。
senses.why: The quarrel picture is the oldest one: someone comes between two raised fists.
senses.whyCN: 劝架的图像最古老：有人走到两只举起的手之间。

intro.en: Intervention is the Latin action noun on intervenire, to come in between.
intro.cn: intervention 是建立在 intervenire（来到中间）上的拉丁语动作名词。

items.en: Venire meant to come; intervenire meant to come between.
items.cn: venire 意为「来」，intervenire 意为「来到中间」。

items.en: Interventio was used for a coming in between two events.
items.cn: interventio 用于指两个事件之间的插入。

items.en: French intervention carried the sense into legal procedure.
items.cn: 法语 intervention 把这个意思带入法律程序。

items.en: English used it for a third party entering a case.
items.cn: 英语用它指第三方进入案件。

items.en: Modern states and clinics made it a term of policy and care.
items.cn: 现代国家与诊所使它成为政策与医疗用语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -vent- coming stem; the near-meaning group holds other words for stepping in.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -vent-「来」词干；近义组收其他表示插手的词。

entries.definition: The verb of coming in between.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「干预」。

entries.definition: One who favours stepping in.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「干预主义者」。

entries.definition: Something newly thought up.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「发明」，拼写相近。

entries.definition: Unwanted meddling in another's affairs.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「干涉」，多含贬义。

entries.definition: Helping two sides settle a dispute.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「调解」，重在促成和解。

entries.definition: The state of taking part in something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「参与」，语气中性。

normalIntro.en: These hooks place the word at the moment an extra chair appears at the table.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把它放在「桌边忽然多出一把椅子」的那一刻。

normal.en: -tion turns intervene into a countable act.
normal.cn: -tion 把 intervene 变成可数的行为。

normal.en: Early intervention is the phrase doctors and teachers share.
normal.cn: early intervention 是医生和老师共用的说法。

normal.en: Government intervention changes markets from outside.
normal.cn: government intervention 从外部改变市场。

normal.en: The word keeps venire, the coming of convene and prevent.
normal.cn: 这个词保留 venire，即 convene 与 prevent 里的「来」。

normal.en: Intervention arrives before anyone has asked for it.
normal.cn: intervention 往往在没人开口请求时就到了。

abstract.en: Intervention is a third hand on a two-hand knot.
abstract.cn: 干预是第三只手去解两个人的结。

abstract.en: To intervene is to decide that waiting is no longer a plan.
abstract.cn: 介入等于判定：再等下去已不算计划。

abstract.en: The kindest intervention can look like an interruption.
abstract.cn: 最善意的介入也可能像一次打断。

examples.en: The report called for intervention by the health ministry.
examples.cn: 报告呼吁卫生部介入。

examples.en: Without prompt intervention the injury would have worsened.
examples.cn: 若不及时介入，伤势会更严重。

examples.en: Their intervention in the market was widely criticised.
examples.cn: 他们对市场的干预受到广泛批评。

dict_mnemonic.text: intervene（走到中间）+ tion（名词）——插到中间这件事

root: 拉丁语 venire「来」→ intervenire「来到中间」→ interventio「介入」→ 古法语 → 英语 intervention。同族有 intervene、convention、prevention。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: outside action, professional help, and stepping into a conflict.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：外部行动、专业救助，以及进入冲突把人拉开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an extra chair placed at the middle of a table set for two.
core.cn: 核心意象：为两人摆好的桌子正中多出的一把椅子。

branches.en: THE COURT: an outside power changes the outcome.
branches.cn: 法院这条线：外部力量改变结果。

branches.en: THE CLINIC: help offered early and on purpose.
branches.cn: 诊所这条线：越早越好的有意帮助。

branches.en: THE FIST: two fighters pulled apart.
branches.cn: 拳头这条线：两个正要动手的人被拉开。

branches.en: THE LINK: both begin with someone not invited in.
branches.cn: 连接线：两个义项都始于一个未被邀请者到场。

branches.en: THE AIM: helping and stopping share the same goal of less harm.
branches.cn: 目标线：救助与制止都指向更少的伤害。

intro.en: Intervention is inter- plus the root vent- "come" and the noun ending -ion.
intro.cn: intervention 由 inter- 加词根 vent-「来」与名词词尾 -ion 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin interventio and intervenire are recorded members of this family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 interventio 与 intervenire 都是这一族的记载形式。

items.example: The root also appears in event and adventure.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也见于 event 与 adventure。

items.example: The noun is the direct source.
The verb is the base of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是名词的基础。

items.example: It builds convention from the same root.
items.exampleCN: 它用同一词根构成 convention。

definition_zh: 唯一的；独家的；脚底；鞋底
definition_en: only or single, belonging to one person or group, or the bottom of a foot or shoe
core_image: 一双鞋中只有一双鞋底磨破了
scene: 他是家里唯一的经济来源。 He is the sole earner in the family.
sceneCN: 这里 sole 是「唯一的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他是家里唯一的经济来源。

derivatives.zh: 仅仅；唯一地
个体经营者

senses.title: Only one
senses.definition: being the only one of its kind or the only person involved
senses.definitionCN: 同类中唯一的，或唯一涉及的人
senses.example: He is the sole earner in the family.
senses.exampleCN: 他是家里唯一的经济来源。
senses.why: This is the central adjective sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心的形容词义项。

senses.title: Belonging to one
senses.definition: belonging to or controlled by one person or group
senses.definitionCN: 属于或由一个人、一个团体控制的
senses.example: The firm is the sole agent for the brand.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司是该品牌的独家代理。
senses.why: Exclusivity is the commercial form of being alone.
senses.whyCN: 独家性是「唯一」的商业形式。

senses.title: Bottom of a foot
senses.definition: the bottom surface of a foot or a shoe
senses.definitionCN: 脚或鞋的底面
senses.example: There is a hole in the sole of my shoe.
senses.exampleCN: 我鞋底破了个洞。
senses.why: A separate noun names the underside.
senses.whyCN: 一个单独的名词指底面。

intro.en: Sole joins two Latin words: one for alone and one for a sandal.
intro.cn: sole 合并了两个拉丁词：一个表示独自，一个表示凉鞋。

items.en: Solus meant alone or only.
items.cn: solus 意为独自或唯一。

items.en: Solea meant a sandal or the bottom of a shoe.
items.cn: solea 意为凉鞋或鞋底。

items.en: Sole carried both the adjective and the foot sense.
items.cn: sole 同时承载形容词义和脚底义。

items.en: The word entered English in both senses.
items.cn: 这个词以两个义项进入英语。

items.en: The adjective extended to exclusive commercial rights.
items.cn: 形容词义扩展到独家商业权利。

note.en: Sole is compared with look-alike words and words for being the only one.
note.cn: 把 sole 与形近词以及表示唯一性的词作比较。

entries.definition: the spiritual part of a person
entries.definitionCN: 灵魂

entries.definition: the earth where plants grow
entries.definitionCN: 土壤

entries.definition: hard and firm
entries.definitionCN: 固体的；结实的

entries.definition: single and no other
entries.definitionCN: 唯一的

entries.definition: one and not more
entries.definitionCN: 单一的

entries.definition: limited to one person or group
entries.definitionCN: 独家的

normalIntro.en: Sole means one and no other, or the one surface that meets the ground.
normalIntro.cn: sole 意为只有一个、没有别的，或接触地面的那个底面。

normal.en: He is the sole earner in the family.
normal.cn: 他是家里唯一的经济来源。

normal.en: The firm is the sole agent for the brand.
normal.cn: 这家公司是该品牌的独家代理。

normal.en: There is a hole in the sole of my shoe.

normal.en: Her sole purpose was to finish the race.

normal.en: The sole owner signed the papers.
normal.cn: 唯一的所有者签了文件。

abstract.en: What is sole carries both privilege and loneliness.
abstract.cn: 唯一之物既带来特权，也带来孤独。

abstract.en: The part that touches the ground is rarely seen.
abstract.cn: 接触地面的部分很少被看见。

abstract.en: One responsibility cannot be divided among many.
abstract.cn: 一份责任无法分给许多人。

examples.cn: 他是家里唯一的经济来源。

examples.en: There is a hole in the sole of my shoe.

dict_mnemonic.text: sole 与 soul 同音，与 soil 形近；sole purpose 是「唯一目的」，the sole of the shoe 是「鞋底」。

root: 形容词义来自拉丁语 solus（独自），名词义来自拉丁语 solea（凉鞋、鞋底），两源同形合并于英语。

sensesIntro.en: Sole means only one, belonging to one party, or the bottom of a foot or shoe.
sensesIntro.cn: sole 意为唯一的、独家专有的，或脚底、鞋底。

core.en: One alone, or the one surface below.
core.cn: 独自一个，或下方唯一的表面。

branches.en: One person carries the whole duty.
branches.cn: 一个人承担全部责任。

branches.en: One company holds the only rights.
branches.cn: 一家公司掌握独家权利。

branches.en: The shoe touches the road below.
branches.cn: 鞋底接触下方的路面。

branches.en: Being alone and being exclusive share one adjective.
branches.cn: 独自与独家共用一个形容词。

branches.en: The word for one also names a single surface.
branches.cn: 表示唯一的词也指一个单一的表面。

intro.en: Sole builds words for single ownership and for the underside of a shoe.
intro.cn: sole 构成表示单一所有权和鞋底的词。

latinIntro.en: The adjective comes from Latin solus, meaning alone.
latinIntro.cn: 形容词义来自拉丁语 solus，意为独自。

items.meaning: the only agent for a product

items.meaning: the bottom surface of a shoe

definition_zh: 团块；大量、大批；质量；群众、大众；弥撒；聚集、集结
definition_en: a large shapeless body of matter, a great quantity of it, or the amount of matter in a body
core_image: 一盆揉好的面团被两只手按下去，整团摊在案板上，越揉越沉
scene: 面粉加水和成一大团，摊在案板上占了半张台面，两只手按下去要费点力。 A mass of dough filled the whole board.
sceneCN: 这里 mass 指没有定形、聚成整体的一大团东西（第 1 个义项：不分形状的团块）；句意：一大团面团占满了整块案板。图中可辨识物件：面团、案板、面粉袋、擀面杖；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 团块；大量；质量；群众；弥撒

forms.label: 单数（物质义通常不可数）

derivatives.zh: 巨大的；大量的
极大地；大规模地
无质量的
生物量；生物质
面向大众市场的

senses.title: A shapeless lump
senses.definition: a body of matter with no clear shape, often formed by pressing things together
senses.definitionCN: 没有明确形状的一团物质，常由挤压而成
senses.example: A mass of dough filled the whole board.
senses.exampleCN: 一大团面团占满了整块案板。
senses.why: Latin massa meant a lump of dough or metal, so the shapeless lump is the root picture of the word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 massa 指面团或金属的一团，因此「无定形的一团」是这个词的根源画面。

senses.title: A very large quantity
senses.definition: a great number or amount of things taken together
senses.definitionCN: 许多事物合在一起所形成的大数量
senses.example: A mass of evidence supports the claim.
senses.exampleCN: 大量证据支持这一主张。
senses.why: a lump is many small pieces pressed into one, so the word naturally shifted from one lump to a heap of things.
senses.whyCN: 一团是许多小块压在一起，于是这个词自然从「一团」滑到「一堆」。

senses.title: Quantity of matter in physics
senses.definition: the quantity of matter in a body, measured by its resistance to acceleration
senses.definitionCN: 物体所含物质的量，以其抵抗加速度的程度来量度
senses.example: Mass is not the same as weight, though scales blur the two.
senses.exampleCN: 质量与重量并不相同，尽管秤常把两者混在一起。
senses.why: physicists needed a word for how much stuff a body contains, and the lump word was the obvious choice.
senses.whyCN: 物理学家需要指称一个物体含有多少实体，那团东西的词自然是首选。

senses.title: The common people
senses.definition: the ordinary people of a society, considered as one body
senses.definitionCN: 社会中的普通人，被当作一个整体来看
senses.example: The reform was popular with the masses but not with the owners.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革受大众欢迎，却不受业主欢迎。
senses.why: crowds pressed together in a square look like one lump, and politics named that lump the masses.
senses.whyCN: 广场上挤在一起的人群看上去就是一团，政治语言把这团叫作「大众」。

senses.title: The religious service
senses.definition: the central service of the Roman Catholic Church, especially one said for the dead
senses.definitionCN: 罗马天主教会的主要礼仪，尤指为亡者举行的那一场
senses.example: They attended early Mass on Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 他们星期天参加了清早的弥撒。
senses.why: this sense comes from Latin missa 'dismissal', a different source from massa, and must never be merged with the lump word.
senses.whyCN: 这一义出自拉丁 missa「遣散」，与 massa 不同源，绝不能与「团块」那个词混为一谈。

senses.title: To gather in a crowd
senses.definition: to come together in large numbers, as troops or protesters do
senses.definitionCN: 以大量人数聚拢，如军队或抗议者
senses.example: Troops massed along the border overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 部队一夜之间集结在边境一带。
senses.why: if a mass is many units pressed into one body, then to mass is the act of pressing them together.
senses.whyCN: 既然 mass 是许多单位压成一个整体，那么动词 mass 就是把它们压到一起的动作。

senses.title: Large-scale, for everyone
senses.definition: produced or done on a large scale and aimed at ordinary people
senses.definitionCN: 以大规模制作或进行、面向普通人的
senses.example: Mass production brought the clock within reach of clerks.
senses.exampleCN: 大批量生产让职员也买得起钟表。
senses.why: the adjective turns the lump into a scale word: one lump, then one industry serving a whole market.
senses.whyCN: 形容词把「一团」变成尺度词：先是一团，再是整个服务一方市场的产业。

senses.title: The bulk or greater part
senses.definition: the greater part of something, considered as one undifferentiated body
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的较大部分，被看作一个未加区分的整体
senses.example: The mass of the population lives along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 人口的大部分住在沿海一带。
senses.why: a lump is undivided, so the word also covers the majority when nobody bothers to split it up.
senses.whyCN: 一团是不加分割的，因此当没人去细分时，这个词也指「大多数」。

intro.en: Mass in the sense of a lump comes from Latin massa, generally thought to come from Greek maza 'barley cake'. The church sense comes from Latin missa 'dismissal' and is a separate word.
intro.cn: 「团块」义的 mass 来自拉丁 massa，一般认为源自希腊 maza「大麦饼」；弥撒义来自拉丁 missa「遣散」，是另一个词。

items.en: Maza meant a barley cake or a lump of kneaded dough, and it is generally thought to be the older source behind Latin massa.
items.cn: maza 指大麦饼或揉成团的面，一般认为它是拉丁 massa 更早的来源。

items.en: Massa meant a lump, a mass of metal or dough; the further link to Greek maza is a common view rather than a documented chain.
items.cn: massa 指一团、一块金属或面团；它与希腊 maza 的联系是常见看法，而非有文献可查的链条。

items.en: Missa meant 'dismissal' and became the name of the church service; it has nothing to do with massa and must be kept apart.
items.cn: missa 意为「遣散」，后来成为礼拜仪式的名称；它与 massa 毫无关系，必须分开。

items.en: Both words entered English in the Middle Ages, the lump word through French and the church word through the liturgy.
items.cn: 两个词都在中世纪进入英语：团块义经法语而来，礼仪义经教会用语而来。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the lump word was narrowed by physics to the measurable quantity of matter in a body.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，物理学把「团块」词收窄为物体中可量度的物质的量。

items.en: The first dates for the political and industrial senses are approximate; both words are well attested from the Middle Ages.
items.cn: 政治义与工业义的最早年代为约数；两个词在中世纪都已有充分书证。

note.en: The first group holds forms built on massa plus two near-forms, one of which is famously a different word; the second group holds quantity words.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 massa 的词形，另加一个形近但著名地属于另一个词的词；第二组是表示数量的词。

entries.definition: Built on mass with an adjective suffix, meaning 'huge and solid'; it describes the lump rather than naming it.
entries.definitionCN: 在 mass 上加形容词后缀构成，意为「巨大而结实的」；它描述那团东西而不命名它。

entries.definition: A compact group of mountains, from French massif and the same massa stock; it is a shaped lump of rock.
entries.definitionCN: 指紧凑的一群山，出自法语 massif 与同一 massa 词源；它是被塑造过的一团岩石。

entries.definition: From French amasser, built on masse; to heap things into one lump, usually wealth or evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 出自法语 amasser，由 masse 构成；把东西堆成一团，通常指财富或证据。

entries.definition: The volume or the greater part of something; mass stresses the stuff, bulk stresses the size it takes up.
entries.definitionCN: 指体积或较大部分；mass 强调那团实体，bulk 强调它占的空间。

entries.definition: A pile of separate things stacked up; a mass can be one continuous body, a heap is always many pieces.
entries.definitionCN: 分开的东西堆成一摞；mass 可以是一个连续的整体，heap 永远是许多件。

entries.definition: A large number of people gathered together; the phrase for the masses is a political body, not a crowd in a street.
entries.definitionCN: 聚在一起的一大群人；「大众」是政治意义上的整体，不是街上的一群人。

entries.definition: The force of gravity on a body; mass is how much matter it holds, weight is how hard gravity pulls it.
entries.definitionCN: 重力对物体施加的力；mass 是所含物质的量，weight 是重力拉它的力度。

entries.definition: More than half of a counted group; the bulk phrase means an unsplit body, not a tally.
entries.definitionCN: 被计数群体中过半的部分；而「人口的大部分」是不加细分的整体，不是点数结果。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin source, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁来源、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Latin massa was a lump of dough, so mass begins as a shapeless lump.
normal.cn: 拉丁 massa 是一团面，因此 mass 最初就是无定形的一团。

normal.en: The family runs mass, massive, massively, massless and biomass.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 mass、massive、massively、massless 与 biomass。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the scale sense: mass media, mass production, mass market.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出规模义：大众传媒、大批量生产、大众市场。

normal.en: Physics pairs mass with weight, and the two are not interchangeable.
normal.cn: 物理把 mass 与 weight 配对，二者不能互换。

normal.en: Remember that Mass the service comes from Latin missa, not from massa.
normal.cn: 要记住弥撒义的 Mass 出自拉丁 missa，而非 massa。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd in a square pressing into one single dark shape from above.
abstract.cn: 从高处看，广场上的人群挤成一个黑色整体。

abstract.en: Picture a snowball rolling downhill and growing heavier with every turn.
abstract.cn: 想象一个雪球滚下山坡，每转一圈就更沉一些。

abstract.en: Picture a baker's hands pushing a whole table of dough into one lump.
abstract.cn: 想象面包师把整张台面的面按成一团。

examples.en: The nebula contains a mass of gas several times that of the sun.
examples.cn: 这团星云所含气体的质量是太阳的若干倍。

examples.en: Mass tourism has changed the old harbour beyond recognition.
examples.cn: 大众旅游把这个老港口改变得面目全非。

examples.en: Protesters massed outside the hall before the vote.
examples.cn: 表决之前，抗议者在大厅外集结。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马死」——一大群马挤成一团，马死了也堆成一大堆 → 团块、大量

root: 希腊 maza「大麦饼、面团」→ 拉丁 massa「一团、一块」→ 法语 masse → 英语 mass「团块、大量」；物理学再收窄为「质量」；弥撒义的 Mass 另出拉丁 missa「遣散」，与此无关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all begin with one lump: dough on a board, a heap of evidence, a measured quantity in physics, a crowd pressed into one body, the bulk of a population, the act of pressing a crowd together, an industry serving everyone, and an unsplit majority.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从一团东西出发：案板上的面团、一堆证据、物理里可量度的量、挤成一个整体的人群、人口的大部分、把人挤到一起的动作、服务所有人的产业，以及不加细分的多数。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lump of dough pressed flat across a whole board.
core.cn: 核心意象：一团面被按平，摊满整块案板。

branches.en: THE LUMP AND THE HEAP: one continuous body first, then many pieces pressed into a great quantity.
branches.cn: 一团与一堆：先是连续的一体，再是许多件压成大数量。

branches.en: THE MEASURED LUMP: physics turns the lump into a number that resists acceleration.
branches.cn: 可量度的团：物理学把这团东西变成一个抵抗加速度的数。

branches.en: PEOPLE AS ONE BODY: a crowd pressed together becomes the masses, and an unsplit bulk becomes the majority.
branches.cn: 被当作一体的民众：挤在一起的人群成为大众，未加细分的整体成为多数。

branches.en: THE OTHER WORD: the church service sounds the same but descends from missa, a root of its own.
branches.cn: 另一个词：宗教礼仪读音相同，却出自 missa，自有一个词根。

branches.en: THE ACT AND THE SCALE: pressing things together, and an industry that serves a whole market.
branches.cn: 动作与尺度：把东西压到一起，以及服务整个市场的产业。

intro.en: Mass is a Latin noun of a lump, with a small English family built on it; the church word Mass is a separate stock and is marked as such.
intro.cn: mass 是拉丁语里表示「一团」的名词，英语在其上长出一个不大的词族；弥撒义的 Mass 另有来源，下面单独标出。

latinIntro.en: Latin massa gives mass, massive, massif and amass through French; missa is a different Latin noun and gives only the church sense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 massa 经法语给出 mass、massive、massif 与 amass；missa 是另一个拉丁名词，只给出礼仪义。

items.meaning: lump; mass of metal or dough
items.meaningCN: 一团；金属或面团的一块
items.example: The root supplies the picture of a shapeless lump.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「无定形一团」的画面。

items.example: One word covers the lump, the heap and the measured quantity.
items.exampleCN: 同一个词兼指团块、堆与可量度的量。

items.example: A massive wall is one great lump of stone.
items.exampleCN: 一堵厚墙就是一大团石头。

items.example: The massif rises as one block from the plain.
items.exampleCN: 那片山地从平原上整块隆起。

items.example: To amass is to press many things into one heap.
items.exampleCN: amass 就是把许多东西压成一堆。

items.meaning: the total living matter in an area
items.meaningCN: 某一区域内的生物总量
items.example: The prefix narrows the lump to living stuff.
items.exampleCN: 前缀把这团东西限定为活物。

items.example: The compound turns the lump into a sales scale.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把「一团」变成销售的尺度。

items.structure: Latin noun, first declension, separate source
items.example: This root is not related to massa in any way.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根与 massa 没有任何关系。

definition_zh: 制造商；生产商；厂商
definition_en: a company or person that makes goods from raw materials, especially in large quantities
core_image: 展会现场，一家工厂的展台上摆着自家生产的电机，名片上只印着工厂的名字
scene: 展会现场，一家工厂的展台上摆着自家生产的电机，名片上只印着工厂名。 The manufacturer recalled twelve thousand units after a fault appeared in the field.
sceneCN: 句中的说法指「生产这些商品的工厂或公司」（第 1 个义项：以原料批量生产商品的企业）；句意为现场出现故障后，制造商召回了十二万台产品。图中可辨识物件：展台、电机、名片、召回通知单；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 厂商；品牌所有者（相对零售商）

derivatives.zh: 制造；制成品
制造业；制造的
制成的；人造的
可制造的

senses.title: A firm that makes goods
senses.titleCN: 制造商品的工厂或公司
senses.definition: a business that turns raw materials or parts into finished products
senses.definitionCN: 把原料或零件变成成品的企业
senses.example: The manufacturer recalled twelve thousand units after a fault appeared in the field.
senses.exampleCN: 现场出现故障后，制造商召回了十二万台产品。
senses.why: The agent suffix marks the doer of the verb, so the maker of goods is simply the one who manufactures.
senses.whyCN: 施动后缀标记动作的执行者，因此生产商品者就是执行「制造」的那一方。

senses.title: The brand owner, as against the shop
senses.titleCN: 与零售商相对的品牌厂商
senses.definition: the party responsible for the product's design and warranty, in contrast to the retailer
senses.definitionCN: 对产品设计与保修负责、与零售商相对的一方
senses.example: Retailers pass warranty claims back to the manufacturer.
senses.exampleCN: 零售商把保修索赔转回给厂商。
senses.why: Liability and warranty follow the maker rather than the seller, which fixes this legal-commercial sense.
senses.whyCN: 责任与保修跟着生产者而不是销售者，这固定了这层法律与商业含义。

senses.title: A maker of machinery
senses.definition: a firm that builds machines or equipment for other businesses
senses.definitionCN: 为其他企业建造机器或设备的企业
senses.example: The press manufacturer sends an engineer for every installation.
senses.exampleCN: 压机制造商每次安装都会派一名工程师。
senses.why: Industrial buyers speak of the firm that built the machine as its manufacturer, even when it makes nothing else.
senses.whyCN: 工业买家把造这台机器的企业称为它的制造商，即使它不做别的产品。

senses.title: A car maker
senses.definition: a company that assembles vehicles and sells them under its own name
senses.definitionCN: 组装车辆并以自己名义出售的公司
senses.example: Three car manufacturers share one battery plant.
senses.exampleCN: 三家汽车制造商共用一座电池工厂。
senses.why: In vehicles the assembler is treated as the maker even though most parts come from elsewhere.
senses.whyCN: 在汽车业，即使大部分零件来自别处，组装者仍被视为制造者。

senses.title: A drug maker
senses.definition: a company that produces medicines and holds the licence for them
senses.definitionCN: 生产药品并持有相关许可的公司
senses.example: The drug manufacturer filed for approval in two markets.
senses.exampleCN: 这家药品生产商在两个市场申请了批准。
senses.why: Regulated products need a named responsible firm, and that firm is called the manufacturer in law.
senses.whyCN: 受管制产品需要一个具名的责任企业，法律上这家企业就称为制造商。

senses.title: A contract maker for another brand
senses.titleCN: 为他人品牌代工的生产商
senses.definition: a firm that builds goods to another company's specification and brand
senses.definitionCN: 按另一家公司的规格与品牌生产商品的企业
senses.example: As an original equipment manufacturer, it builds parts to a client's drawing.
senses.exampleCN: 作为原始设备制造商，它按客户的图纸生产零件。
senses.why: When design and brand belong to one firm and production to another, the producer is still the manufacturer of record.
senses.whyCN: 当设计与品牌属一家、生产属另一家时，生产方仍是名义上的制造商。

senses.title: An employer in wage talks
senses.titleCN: 劳资语境中的制造企业
senses.definition: factory owners taken together as the employing side in negotiations
senses.definitionCN: 在谈判中被当作雇主一方的工厂所有者整体
senses.example: The manufacturers and the union reached a wage deal.
senses.exampleCN: 制造企业与工会达成了工资协议。
senses.why: In labour disputes a whole group of firms is addressed as one party, and the trade name stands for the employers.
senses.whyCN: 在劳资争议中，一群企业被当作一方来对话，行业称呼便代表雇主。

senses.title: The responsible party in product law
senses.definition: the party legally answerable for a defect in a product, whatever the chain of sale
senses.definitionCN: 不论销售链条如何，对产品缺陷负法律责任的一方
senses.example: Liability falls on the manufacturer, not the shop.
senses.exampleCN: 责任落在制造商身上，而不是店铺。
senses.why: Product liability law needs one identifiable party at the origin, and that party is the manufacturer.
senses.whyCN: 产品责任法需要在源头有一个可辨认的责任方，这个责任方就是制造商。

intro.en: Manufacturer is the maker-noun of a French-derived verb, with an English agent suffix added. The Latin base means 'made by hand'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这是一个法语来源动词的施动名词，加上了英语表示「做者」的后缀。其拉丁底子意为「用手做成」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Manus 'hand' supplies the first half; its deeper root is reconstructed, so source uncertain below Latin.
items.cn: manus「手」提供前半；其更深词根属重构形式，故拉丁语以下来源不确定。

items.en: Facere 'to make' supplies the second half, and its pre-Latin root is also reconstructed.
items.cn: facere「制作」提供后半，其在拉丁语之前的词根同样属重构形式。

items.en: The phrase meant 'made by hand' and passed through French as a noun for goods and for the making of them.
items.cn: 这个短语意为「用手做成」，经法语成为指商品及其制作的名词。

items.en: French manufacture named the making and the thing made; English borrowed both in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 法语 manufacture 兼指制作与制品，英语在十七世纪两者都借入。

items.en: English added its suffix for the person or firm that performs an action, and from the eighteenth century manufacturer meant the maker of goods.
items.cn: 英语加上表示动作执行者（人或企业）的后缀，自十八世纪起这个词指商品制造者。

note.en: Group one holds forms built on the same verb; group two holds names for the parties that make or supply goods.
note.cn: 第一组是同出该动词的各种形式；第二组是表示制造或供应商品一方的名称。

entries.definition: The verb and the act of making, not the firm; without the agent suffix there is no doer.
entries.definitionCN: 指制造的动词与动作，而非企业；没有施动后缀就没有「做者」。

entries.definition: The ongoing activity or the sector, with no reference to a particular company.
entries.definitionCN: 指持续的活动或整个部门，不特指某家公司。

entries.definition: Describes goods made in a factory, or an excuse invented; it says nothing about who made them.
entries.definitionCN: 描述工厂制成的商品或编造的借口，不说明是谁造的。

entries.definition: An old word for a factory building; a manufacturer is the firm, a manufactory is the place.
entries.definitionCN: 指工厂建筑的旧词；制造商是企业，工场是地点。

entries.definition: Anyone who makes goods, films or energy; it is wider than a factory firm.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指制造商品、影片或能源的一方，比工厂企业更宽。

entries.definition: The everyday word for the one who makes something, often a craftsperson or a brand.
entries.definitionCN: 指制作某物的日常词，常指手艺人或品牌。

entries.definition: A firm that provides parts or materials to the maker rather than making the final good.
entries.definitionCN: 向制造者提供零件或材料、而非生产最终产品的企业。

entries.definition: A seller of goods, often the party that faces the buyer.
entries.definitionCN: 商品的销售方，常指面对买家的一方。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: A verb for making goods plus the suffix for the one who does it: the firm that does the making.
normal.cn: 表示制造商品的动词加「做者」后缀：做这件事的企业。

normal.en: The family runs manufacture, manufacturing, manufactured and the adjective for what can be made.
normal.cn: 同族词包括制造、制造业、制成的，以及表示可制造的形容词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: original equipment manufacturer, car manufacturer, drug manufacturer, warranty.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出领域：原始设备制造商、汽车制造商、药品生产商、厂商保修。

normal.en: The word appears in three roles: the maker, the brand owner behind the shop, and the party liable for a defect.
normal.cn: 这个词出现在三种角色里：制造者、店铺背后的品牌方，以及对缺陷负责的一方。

normal.en: A firm that designs nothing may still be called the manufacturer if it builds the goods.
normal.cn: 一家不设计任何东西的企业，只要它把商品做出来，仍可能被称为制造商。

abstract.en: Picture a nameplate on a machine with only a factory name on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一台机器的铭牌上只印着一个厂名。

abstract.en: Picture a shop handing a broken item back up the chain.
abstract.cn: 想象店铺把坏掉的物件沿链条往回递。

abstract.en: Picture one shed building parts for three different badges.
abstract.cn: 想象一座厂房为三个不同商标造零件。

examples.en: The manufacturer tested every batch before shipping.
examples.cn: 制造商在发货前检测了每一批。

examples.en: A small manufacturer can rarely afford its own retail network.
examples.cn: 小型制造商很少有能力自建零售网络。

examples.en: Under the contract, the manufacturer owns the tooling.
examples.cn: 按合同，模具归制造商所有。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「manufacture（制造）+ er（做的人/厂）」——做东西的那一方 → 制造商、厂商

root: 法语来源的「制造」动词加英语施动后缀构成；该动词的拉丁底子是「手」与「做」组合成的「用手做成」短语，两个词根更早的来源均属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one firm: it makes goods, it stands behind the brand, it builds machines, it assembles cars, it holds a drug licence, it builds for another's label, it faces the union, and it answers for defects.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一家企业展开：它做商品、站在品牌背后、造机器、组装汽车、持有药品许可、替他人商标代工、面对工会，最后对缺陷负责。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a booth at a trade fair with a motor on a plinth and a card that carries only the factory's name.
core.cn: 核心意象：展会上的一个展台，台座上摆着一台电机，名片上只印着厂名。

chain: THE NAME SITS ON THE GOODS
THE NAME ANSWERS FOR THE GOODS

branches.en: THE MAKER: making goods and building machines are the same doer in different trades.
branches.cn: 制造者：做商品与造机器，是同一施动者处在不同行业。

branches.en: THE RESPONSIBLE NAME: the brand owner behind the shop and the licensed drug maker are both the party on record.
branches.cn: 具名的责任方：店铺背后的品牌方与持证的药品生产商，都是名义上负责的一方。

branches.en: THE ASSEMBLER: a car maker and a contract builder both put their name to goods designed elsewhere.
branches.cn: 组装者：汽车制造商与代工生产商，都把名字落到别处设计的商品上。

branches.en: THE EMPLOYER: in wage talks a group of firms speaks as one party.
branches.cn: 雇主：在工资谈判中，一群企业作为一方发言。

branches.en: THE LIABLE PARTY: product law follows the maker to the origin of the goods.
branches.cn: 责任方：产品责任法沿制造者追到商品的源头。

intro.en: Manufacturer is a Latin-rooted verb of making plus an English suffix for the doer, so it reads as hand, making, and the one who makes.
intro.cn: 这是一个拉丁词根的「制作」动词加英语表示「做者」的后缀，因此可读作「手」「制作」与「做这件事的一方」。

latinIntro.en: Latin manus 'hand' and facere 'make' combine in the phrase for made by hand, which French turned into a noun; English added the agent suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语「手」与「做」组合成「用手做成」的短语，法语把它变成名词，英语再加上施动后缀。

items.example: The hand is the original instrument of making.

items.structure: facere, feci, factum (Latin verb, third conjugation)

items.example: French compressed the phrase into one noun and verb.
items.exampleCN: 法语把这个短语压缩成一个名词兼动词。

items.example: The suffix turns the action into a doer.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动作变成施动者。

items.example: The doer here is a company, not a person.
items.exampleCN: 这里的施动者是公司，而不是个人。

items.example: The process noun has no doer in it.
items.exampleCN: 这个表示过程的名词不含施动者。

items.example: The suffix marks what the process allows.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标记工艺上的可行性。

definition_zh: 愚蠢的；傻的；疯癫的
definition_en: silly or foolish; (British, informal) crazy or senseless
core_image: 拍脑门的傻气：明摆着的事偏要做反
scene: 他把伞留在家，冒着瓢泼大雨走了整条街。" Don't be daft—take my umbrella!" his neighbour shouted.
sceneCN: 这里 daft 是「傻的、愚蠢的」（第 1 个义项：做事不明智的傻气）；句意是邻居骂他傻，让他拿伞。

pos.zh: 愚蠢的；傻的；（英式口语）疯疯癫癫的

derivatives.zh: 由 daft 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「傻乎乎地」
由 daft 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「愚蠢；傻气」

senses.title: Foolish or silly in behaviour
senses.definition: acting in a silly way that shows poor judgement
senses.definitionCN: 行事傻气、判断力差的
senses.example: It was daft to leave the windows open in a storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴雨天开着窗户真傻。
senses.why: The original sense was gentle or meek; English shifted it to harmless silliness.
senses.whyCN: 该词原义是「温顺」，英语里逐渐偏移为无害的傻气、不明智。

senses.title: Crazy or insane (British informal)
senses.definition: behaving as if out of one's mind; slightly mad
senses.definitionCN: 举止像失去理智似的，有点疯
senses.example: The noise from the construction site is driving me daft.
senses.exampleCN: 工地的噪音快把我逼疯了。
senses.why: Silliness pushed one step further becomes madness; the mild word can climb to the strong sense.
senses.whyCN: 傻气再往前一步就是疯癫，温和的词被推向了强烈的用法。

senses.title: Foolish in a playful, affectionate way
senses.definition: used teasingly about someone you like, without real criticism
senses.definitionCN: 带调侃地形容喜欢的人，并非真的批评
senses.example: You daft old fool, you forgot your own birthday!
senses.exampleCN: 你这个傻老头，把自己的生日都忘了！
senses.why: Because the word stays informal and mild, it works as teasing rather than insult.
senses.whyCN: 因为词感口语而温和，它常被用作玩笑式打趣而非辱骂。

intro.en: Daft began as a word for gentle or meek and slid, over centuries, into foolish and then crazy.
intro.cn: daft 最初表示「温顺、文雅」，历经数百年滑向「愚蠢」，再到「疯癫」。

items.en: Old English gedefe meant gentle, fitting, or meek; the shortened form def(e) survived in Middle English.
items.cn: 古英语 gedefe 意为「温顺、合适」，其截短形式 def(e) 在中古英语中仍在使用。

items.en: Middle English daft first meant gentle or mild, then came to mean foolish or stupid.
items.cn: 中古英语 daft 先表「温和」，随后转为「愚蠢、迟钝」。

items.en: By the 16th–17th centuries the word covered silly behaviour and mild insanity; Shakespeare used it in both flavours.
items.cn: 十六至十七世纪，该词已兼指傻气与轻度疯癫；莎士比亚两种用法都用过。

items.en: In Scottish and Northern English the older senses survived longer, including 'meek' in Scots law contexts.
items.cn: 在苏格兰和英格兰北部方言中，旧义「温顺」保留更久，苏格兰法律用语里仍在使用。

items.en: Today daft is chiefly British informal for silly, with daft as a brush among the best-known idioms.
items.cn: 如今 daft 主要作英式口语「傻的」，习语 daft as a brush 最为著名。

note.en: Watch the spelling daft against draft and raft, and compare its meaning with other silly-words.
note.cn: 注意 daft 与 draft、raft 的拼写区分，并与其它表「傻」的词比较用法。

entries.definition: a preliminary version of a document, or a current of air
entries.definitionCN: 「草稿；气流」，与 daft 仅差一个字母 r，词源不同，只是拼写相近

entries.definition: a flat floating platform of logs
entries.definitionCN: 「木筏」，与 daft 形近，词义无关

entries.definition: skilful and quick with the hands
entries.definitionCN: 「灵巧的」，与 daft 同韵且词形相近，意思却几乎相反

entries.definition: foolish in a light, often endearing way
entries.definitionCN: 「傻的」，语气轻快常带可爱意味，是 daft 最接近的通用对应词

entries.definition: showing lack of good sense
entries.definitionCN: 「愚蠢的」，比 daft 稍正式，强调判断力差

entries.definition: British informal for crazy or angry
entries.definitionCN: 英式口语「疯的；生气的」，在疯癫义上与 daft 相通

normalIntro.en: Anchor daft with its sound shape and its British partners.
normalIntro.cn: 用发音形态和英式搭档记住 daft。

normal.en: daft rhymes with draft; remember: don't draft a daft plan.
normal.cn: daft 与 draft 押韵，可记「别把傻主意写成草案」。

normal.en: Idiom: daft as a brush paints a brush that cannot think.
normal.cn: 习语 daft as a brush（傻得像把刷子）画面感极强。

normal.en: drive someone daft = drive someone mad, same pattern.
normal.cn: drive someone daft 与 drive someone mad 结构相同，可互相替换记忆。

normal.en: Derived pair: daftly (adv.) and daftness (n.) follow the regular pattern.
normal.cn: 派生对：daftly（副词）和 daftness（名词）按规则后缀构成。

normal.en: It is chiefly British: American English prefers silly or dumb.
normal.cn: 该词主要用于英式英语，美式英语更常说 silly 或 dumb。

abstract.en: Picture someone walking into the rain with the umbrella left at home.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人伞落在家里、径直走进大雨的画面。

abstract.en: Feel the flat, blunt sound /dɑːft/ like a wooden clunk on the head.
abstract.cn: 感受 /dɑːft/ 那种平直钝响，像木棍敲头的闷声。

abstract.en: Hear a friend laughing and calling you daft, not angry.
abstract.cn: 耳边是朋友笑着喊你傻，并无恶意。

examples.en: It would be daft to sell the house now, when prices are so low.
examples.cn: 现在房价这么低就卖房子，太傻了。

examples.en: The puppy kept chasing its own tail like a daft little thing.
examples.cn: 小狗一直追自己的尾巴，傻乎乎的。

examples.en: Stop that whistling—it's driving me daft!
examples.cn: 别吹口哨了——快把我逼疯了！

dict_mnemonic.text: 「打夫特」——傻到被人「打」也「特」别憨；谐音仅助记，真实词源是古英语「温顺」义的偏移。

root: 古英语 gedefe（温和的、合适的）经截短与语音演变成为中古英语 daft；原义「温顺」→「迟钝」→「愚蠢」→「疯癫」，属词义贬化，非拉丁语源。

sensesIntro.en: The word moves from plain silliness, up to mild madness, and sideways into affectionate teasing.
sensesIntro.cn: 词义从单纯的傻气爬升到轻度疯癫，又横向转为善意的调侃。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the head-slapping silliness of doing the obvious thing wrong
core.cn: 核心意象：明摆着的事偏做反的拍脑门傻气

branches.en: silly judgement in everyday acts
branches.cn: 日常行为中的傻气判断

branches.en: a daft idea or plan
branches.cn: 愚蠢的主意或计划

branches.en: teasing someone you like
branches.cn: 对喜欢的人的调侃

branches.en: slightly mad behaviour
branches.cn: 疯疯癫癫的举止

branches.en: noise or irritation driving you daft
branches.cn: 噪音或烦扰把人逼疯

intro.en: Daft is a single Germanic adjective; its small family shows regular adjectival derivation.
intro.cn: daft 是单一的日耳曼源形容词；其小词族按规则派生。

latinIntro.en: Daft has no Latin ancestry, coming from Old English gedefe; no Latin relatives are listed.
latinIntro.cn: daft 源自古英语 gedefe，与拉丁语无关，因此不列拉丁同族词。

items.exampleCN: 他傻乎乎地忘了带钥匙。

items.meaningCN: 近义词「傻的」，语感更通用
近义词「疯的」，英式口语中与 daft 互通

items.example: He's daft as a brush but kind.

derivatives.zh: 傻乎乎地
愚蠢；傻气

definition_zh: 谷类作物；谷物；（英式）谷物早餐
definition_en: a grass grown for its edible grain, the grain itself, or a breakfast food made from such grain
core_image: 早餐桌上的一碗燕麦片，旁边放着麦穗与一袋面粉，三样东西都来自同一种草
scene: 厨房台面上摆着一碗泡了牛奶的燕麦片，旁边是一束干麦穗和一袋面粉。 Cereal crops cover more land than any other food group.
sceneCN: 这里指「谷类作物」（第 1 个义项：作为作物类别）；句意为谷类作物占用的土地超过任何其他食物类别。

pos.zh: 谷类作物；谷物；（英式）谷物早餐

derivatives.zh: cereal + grain（组合成分）→ 谷物籽粒（语义偏移：从作物类别缩小到籽粒本身）
cereal + crop（组合成分）→ 谷类作物（语义偏移：强调田间栽培对象）
cereal + bar（组合成分）→ 谷物棒（语义偏移：转为便携食品）
breakfast（早餐）+ cereal → 谷物早餐（语义偏移：专指早餐碗里的加工谷物）
cereal + box（组合成分）→ 谷物包装盒
cereal + bowl（组合成分）→ 谷物碗

senses.title: A grass grown for grain
senses.titleCN: 为收籽粒而种植的禾草
senses.definition: any grass cultivated mainly for its edible starchy grain, such as wheat, rice or maize
senses.definitionCN: 主要为可食淀粉籽粒而栽培的任何禾草，如小麦、稻或玉米
senses.example: Wheat is the cereal best suited to this cold plateau.
senses.exampleCN: 小麦是最适合这块寒冷高原的谷类作物。
senses.why: The word names the plant category, and the botanical link is that all of them are grasses.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名植物类别，其植物学联系在于它们都是禾草。

senses.title: Cereal grain as a mass
senses.definition: the grain of such plants considered as a food or trade commodity
senses.definitionCN: 这类植物的籽粒，作为食品或贸易商品来看
senses.example: Cereal is shipped in bulk from the lake port.
senses.exampleCN: 谷物从这个湖港以散装方式运出。
senses.why: The plant and its product are named by one word because the grain is the reason the plant is grown.
senses.whyCN: 植物与产物用同一个词命名，因为籽粒正是种植它的理由。

senses.title: A breakfast food from grain
senses.definition: a processed breakfast food made from toasted or flaked cereal grains, countable in British usage
senses.definitionCN: 由烘烤或压片的谷物制成的加工早餐食品，英式用法可数
senses.example: The shelf holds six kinds of cereal.
senses.exampleCN: 货架上摆着六种谷物早餐。
senses.why: In the twentieth century the product took the name of its raw material, and British usage made it countable.
senses.whyCN: 二十世纪时产品沿用了原料之名，英式用法又使它可数。

senses.title: A bowl of cereal
senses.definition: a serving of breakfast cereal, usually with milk
senses.definitionCN: 一份谷物早餐，通常加牛奶
senses.example: He eats a bowl of cereal standing up.
senses.exampleCN: 他站着吃一碗谷物早餐。
senses.why: A mass noun can be counted through its container, so a bowl becomes the unit of everyday use.
senses.whyCN: 不可数名词可以借容器计数，于是「一碗」成为日常使用的单位。

senses.title: Grain used as animal feed
senses.definition: cereal grain fed to livestock rather than milled for people
senses.definitionCN: 喂给家畜、而非磨给人吃的谷类籽粒
senses.example: Most of the cereal goes to feed, not to flour.
senses.exampleCN: 大部分谷物用作饲料，而非磨成面粉。
senses.why: The same harvest splits by end use, and feed is the largest destination in many regions.
senses.whyCN: 同一批收成按最终用途分流，在许多地区饲料是最大去向。

senses.title: Adjectival: made from grain
senses.definition: describing a product, field or policy connected with cereal grain
senses.definitionCN: 描述与谷物有关的产品、田地或政策
senses.example: Cereal production rose after the irrigation canal opened.
senses.exampleCN: 灌溉渠开通后谷物产量上升。
senses.why: The noun attributively modifies another noun, a common English way of making a category adjective.
senses.whyCN: 名词作定语修饰另一名词，是英语构成类别形容词的常见方式。

senses.title: A crop in a rotation
senses.definition: a cereal crop considered as one stage in a field rotation
senses.definitionCN: 作为田间轮作一个环节的谷类作物
senses.example: The rotation puts cereal after legumes.
senses.exampleCN: 轮作把谷物安排在豆类之后。
senses.why: Agronomy treats the plant as a slot in a sequence, which gives the word a planning sense.
senses.whyCN: 农学把这种植物当作序列中的一格，于是这个词有了规划义。

senses.title: Grain as a traded commodity
senses.definition: cereal grain priced and traded on markets, often in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 在市场上定价与交易的谷类籽粒，常用复数
senses.example: Cereal prices fell after a record harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 创纪录的收成之后，谷物价格下跌。
senses.why: Trade abstracts the plant into a contract, and the market sense is the most abstract of the eight.
senses.whyCN: 贸易把植物抽象成合约，市场义是八义中最抽象的一层。

intro.en: Cereal comes from Latin cerealis, of Ceres, the Roman goddess of grain, through French céréale. The breakfast sense is a twentieth-century development. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: cereal 来自拉丁 cerealis「刻瑞斯的」，刻瑞斯是罗马谷物女神，经法语 céréale 进入英语。早餐义是二十世纪的发展。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ceres was the Roman goddess of grain and harvest, and her name stands at the head of the whole family.
items.cn: 刻瑞斯是罗马的谷物与丰收女神，她的名字位于整个词族的顶端。

items.en: Cerealis meant of Ceres or of grain, and the neuter plural cerealia named her festival and the grain offered at it.
items.cn: cerealis 意为刻瑞斯的或谷物的；中性复数 cerealia 指她的节庆与节上献的谷物。

items.en: French céréale carried the adjective and noun into English in the nineteenth century as a botanical and agricultural term.
items.cn: 法语 céréale 在十九世纪把这个形容词与名词带入英语，作为植物学与农学术语。

items.en: English cereal first named the grain plants, then their grain, and only later the processed breakfast product.
items.cn: 英语 cereal 先指谷类植物，再指其籽粒，最后才指加工后的早餐产品。

items.en: The breakfast food sense grew in the early twentieth century with commercial flaked and puffed cereals, and British usage made it countable.
items.cn: 早餐食品义在二十世纪初随商业化的压片与膨化谷物而发展，英式用法又使其可数。

items.en: Source uncertain (goddess's deeper name): the pre-Latin origin of Ceres is reconstructed and debated, so any Indo-European root offered for it is a hypothesis.
items.cn: 来源不确定（女神名的更深词源）：Ceres 在拉丁语之前的来源属重构且有争议，凡为其给出的印欧词根均属假说。

note.en: Group one holds words that sound like cereal or name its source; group two holds words for grain and grain foods.
note.cn: 第一组是读音像 cereal 或指其来源的词；第二组是表示谷物及谷物食品的词。

entries.definition: A story or set arranged in a series, from Latin series; it sounds identical to cereal but shares no origin.
entries.definitionCN: 按序列编排的故事或一组事物，来自拉丁 series；与 cereal 读音相同，但无共同来源。

entries.definition: The Roman goddess of grain whose name gives cereal; the word is a proper noun, not a food.
entries.definitionCN: 罗马谷物女神，其名给出 cereal；这是专有名词，不是食物。

entries.definition: The seed of a cereal plant; cereal alone can name the plant, the grain or the breakfast food.
entries.definitionCN: 谷类植物的籽粒；单说 cereal 可指植物、谷物或早餐食品。

entries.definition: The seed or the harvested mass; cereal is the plant category or the breakfast product.
entries.definitionCN: 种子或收获后的总量；cereal 是植物类别或早餐产品。

entries.definition: In British English it means the chief local cereal, often wheat; in American English it means maize. Cereal avoids that split.
entries.definitionCN: 英式英语指当地主要谷物，常为小麦；美式英语指玉米。cereal 可避开这一分歧。

entries.definition: A sweetened mixture of oats, nuts and dried fruit eaten as a breakfast cereal; it is one product, not the category.
entries.definitionCN: 燕麦、坚果与果干加糖混合的早餐谷物食品；它是单一产品，不是类别。

entries.definition: A hot dish of grain boiled in water or milk; cereal is the raw material or the cold packaged product.
entries.definitionCN: 谷物加水或牛奶煮成的热食；cereal 是原料或冷食包装产品。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Ceres, the grain goddess, stands behind the word.
normal.cn: 谷物女神刻瑞斯站在这个词的背后。

normal.en: The family runs cereal, cereal grain, cereal crop, breakfast cereal, cereal bar.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 cereal、cereal grain、cereal crop、breakfast cereal、cereal bar。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: cereal crops in the field, breakfast cereal in the bowl.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分义项：田里的谷类作物，碗里的谷物早餐。

normal.en: The homophone serial belongs to a different family and means a series.
normal.cn: 同音词 serial 属于另一词族，意为系列。

normal.en: British corn and American corn part company, which is why cereal is the safer category word.
normal.cn: 英式 corn 与美式 corn 分道扬镳，因此 cereal 是更安全的类别词。

abstract.en: Picture a goddess holding one sheaf that becomes a bowl, a bag of flour and a box on a shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象一位女神手持一束麦穗，它变成一只碗、一袋面粉与货架上的一盒产品。

abstract.en: Picture a field that is also a price chart, each row of stalks a line on the market page.
abstract.cn: 想象一块田同时是一张价格图，每一行麦秆都是行情页上的一条线。

abstract.en: Picture a breakfast table where every object can be traced back to one kind of grass.
abstract.cn: 想象一张早餐桌，每样东西都能追到同一种草。

examples.en: Cereal crops need nitrogen at the start of the season.
examples.cn: 谷类作物在生长季开始时需要氮。

examples.en: She poured the milk over her cereal.
examples.cn: 她把牛奶倒在谷物早餐上。

examples.en: Cereal prices are sensitive to weather in exporting regions.
examples.cn: 谷物价格对出口地区的天气很敏感。

dict_mnemonic.text: Ceres（谷物女神）+ -al（……的）→ 女神的谷物 → 谷类作物、谷物，再到碗里的谷物早餐；与同音的 serial（系列）无关。

root: 拉丁 Ceres（罗马谷物女神，属格 Cereris）+ -alis「……的」→ cerealis「谷物的」→ 法语 céréale → 英语 cereal；Ceres 的更深词源属重构且有争议。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one grass: the plant, its grain, the milled product, the bowl, the feed, the adjective, the rotation slot and the market contract.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一种草展开：植物、籽粒、加工产品、碗中之物、饲料、形容词、轮作位置与市场合约。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one kind of grass can become a sheaf, a sack of grain, a bag of flour and a bowl on a breakfast table.
core.cn: 核心意象：一种草可以变成一束麦穗、一袋谷粒、一袋面粉和早餐桌上的一只碗。

branches.en: THE PLANT: the botanical category comes first.
branches.cn: 植物：植物学类别最先出现。

branches.en: THE MASS AND THE MARKET: grain as a bulk food and as a priced contract.
branches.cn: 总量与市场：谷物既是散装食品，也是定价合约。

branches.en: THE BOWL: the processed product and the serving it fills.
branches.cn: 碗：加工产品以及它装满的一份。

branches.en: THE FEED TROUGH: the same harvest diverted to animals.
branches.cn: 饲料槽：同一批收成转向动物。

branches.en: THE CATEGORY LABEL: adjective use and the crop's place in a rotation.
branches.cn: 类别标签：形容词用法与作物在轮作中的位置。

intro.en: Cereal is a Latin adjective turned noun, built from a divine name and a suffix, so its morphology runs through the goddess rather than through a verb.
intro.cn: cereal 是由拉丁形容词转成的名词，由一个神名与后缀构成，因此其构词沿女神名展开，而非沿动词展开。

latinIntro.en: Latin Ceres, genitive Cereris, supplies the stem, and -alis makes the relational adjective cerealis; the neuter plural cerealia named the goddess's festival.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 Ceres（属格 Cereris）提供词干，-alis 构成关系形容词 cerealis；中性复数 cerealia 指女神的节庆。

items.structure: Ceres, Cereris (Latin proper noun, third declension)
items.example: Ceres gave her name to the whole category.
items.exampleCN: 刻瑞斯把名字给了整个类别。

items.example: The suffix builds cerealis from the goddess's name.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀由女神名构成 cerealis。

items.example: The adjective described both the goddess and the crop.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词同时描述女神与作物。

items.meaning: a grain plant or its food
items.example: Cereal entered English as a learned term.
items.exampleCN: cereal 作为学术用语进入英语。

items.meaning: the seed of a cereal plant
items.example: The cereal grain is milled into flour.

items.meaning: a cereal grown in a field
items.example: The cereal crop rotated with beans.

items.meaningCN: 加工过的早餐谷物食品
items.example: Breakfast cereal replaced porridge in many homes.
items.exampleCN: 在许多家庭里，谷物早餐取代了粥。

items.example: The cereal bar fits in a coat pocket.
items.exampleCN: 谷物棒能塞进外套口袋。

items.meaning: the packaging of a breakfast cereal
items.example: The cereal box carries the nutrition table.

definition_zh: 游客；观光者；旅游者
definition_en: a person who travels to a place for pleasure rather than work
core_image: 举着地图拍照的人：用脚步画圈的外来客
scene: 广场上人潮涌动，商贩招呼道： The square is full of tourists today.
sceneCN: 这里 tourist 是「游客」（第 1 个义项：观光的人）；句意是商贩感叹今天广场上满是游客。

derivatives.zh: 由 tourist 加 -ic 构成，义为「旅游的；观光业的（较 touristic 常用 touristy）」
由 tourist 加 -y 构成，义为「游客扎堆的；商业观光化的」

senses.title: A pleasure traveler
senses.definition: someone who visits a place for enjoyment, sightseeing, or holiday
senses.definitionCN: 为消遣、观光或度假而到访某地的人
senses.example: Tourists fill the old town every summer.
senses.exampleCN: 每年夏天游客挤满老城。
senses.why: The visitor walks the same loop the word tour names.
senses.whyCN: 观光者走过的正是 tour 所指的那条环线。

senses.title: A user of tourism services
senses.definition: a traveler counted by the tourism industry as a customer
senses.definitionCN: 被旅游业当作顾客统计的出行者
senses.example: The city welcomed ten million tourists last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年这座城市接待了一千万游客。
senses.why: The person becomes the unit the industry counts.
senses.whyCN: 这个人成了行业统计的计量单位。

intro.en: Tourist is tour plus the agent suffix -ist, formed in English in the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: tourist 由 tour 加施动后缀 -ist 构成，十九世纪形成于英语。

items.en: Tornus meant 'circle, lathe', the root of tour.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tornus（圆、车床）是 tour 的词根。

items.en: Tour meant a going-around, later a journey.
items.cn: 古法语 tour 意为绕行，后指旅程。

items.en: Tour settled in English as a circuit journey.
items.cn: 十四世纪 tour 在英语中定型为环程旅行。

items.en: Tourist appeared as railways made pleasure travel common.
items.cn: 十九世纪铁路使观光旅行普及，tourist 一词随之出现。

items.en: Mass tourism made tourist one of the most used travel words.
items.cn: 大众旅游使 tourist 成为最常用的旅行词汇之一。

note.en: Words close to tourist in form, and travelers of other kinds.
note.cn: 与 tourist 形近的词及其他类型的出行者。

entries.definition: the travel industry
entries.definitionCN: 旅游业，与 tourist 同族

entries.definition: a series of contests
entries.definitionCN: 锦标赛，同出「转」的词根（轮流交手）

entries.definition: a person using violence for political aims
entries.definitionCN: 恐怖分子，拼写仅一字母之差，词源完全不同（源自 terror）

entries.definition: anyone who journeys
entries.definitionCN: 旅行者，泛指一切出行之人

entries.definition: one who visits sights
entries.definitionCN: 观光客，侧重看景

entries.definition: a person who visits a place
entries.definitionCN: 访客；来访者的统称

entries.definition: a person living in the place
entries.definitionCN: 居民；常住者，tourist 的反义对照

normalIntro.en: Build the word openly: tour + ist = the one who tours.
normalIntro.cn: 拆开构词来记：tour + ist ＝进行 tour 的人。

normal.en: tourist = tour + -ist, the person who takes the tour
normal.cn: tourist ＝ tour（环程）+ -ist（人），进行环程的人

normal.en: tourist attraction draws tourists
normal.cn: tourist attraction（景点）吸引游客，词组自成回路

normal.en: tourist season means crowded sights
normal.cn: tourist season（旅游旺季）意味着人潮

normal.en: do not confuse with terrorist
normal.cn: 切勿与 terrorist（恐怖分子）混淆，只差一个 o

normal.en: tourist class = the cheapest travel class
normal.cn: tourist class（经济舱）是最低舱位等级

abstract.en: See a figure with a map and camera drawing a loop
abstract.cn: 看一个举着地图相机的人画环线

abstract.en: Hear shutters clicking at every stop of the circle
abstract.cn: 听快门在环线每一站咔嚓作响

abstract.en: Feel the brief stay that never becomes home
abstract.cn: 体会那种永远不会变成家的短暂停留

examples.en: Every tourist should try the local street food.
examples.cn: 每位游客都应该尝尝当地的街头小吃。

examples.en: The tourists asked the guide about the tower's history.
examples.cn: 游客们向导游询问那座塔的历史。

examples.en: Off-season, tourists are few and prices fall.
examples.cn: 淡季游客稀少，价格回落。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「图rist」——脑子里想「图」的 ist（人）：离不开地图的人就是游客。

root: tour（拉丁语 tornus「圆」→ 古法语 tour「绕行」）+ 英语后缀 -ist（从事者）。十九世纪新造词，随大众观光旅行而普及。

sensesIntro.en: The person who walks tour's circle, counted by the industry that serves the circle.
sensesIntro.cn: 走 tour 环线的人，也是服务环线的行业所统计的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stranger with a map drawing a loop
core.cn: 核心意象：举着地图画环线的外来客

branches.en: traveling for pleasure alone
branches.cn: 只为消遣而出行

branches.en: being counted as a customer
branches.cn: 被行业当作顾客计量

branches.en: the same loop from both sides
branches.cn: 同一条环线的两个视角

branches.en: photos and souvenirs as evidence
branches.cn: 照片与纪念品作为环线的证据

branches.en: seasons that swell and empty the loop
branches.cn: 让环线胀缩的淡旺季

intro.en: Tourist shows the living suffix -ist, the maker of person-words.
intro.cn: tourist 展示了能产的后缀 -ist，专造「人」词。

latinIntro.en: The root is Latin tornus through French tour.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是经法语 tour 传来的拉丁语 tornus。

items.meaningCN: 旅行者，近义词而词源不同
观光客，近义词而词源不同
访客，近义词而词源不同
