definition_zh: 迅速的；及时的；准时的；促使；提示；提示符
definition_en: quick and without delay, done at the agreed time, to cause someone to act, or a cue that helps someone carry on
core_image: 有人在旁边轻轻敲一下桌面，另一个人立刻抬头，手上的动作马上跟上来
scene: 排练到一半，演员忘了下一句，场边的人压低声音把词递过去，演员立刻接上。 A stagehand prompted him from the wings, and the scene moved on.
sceneCN: 这里表示「提词、提示」（第 4 个义项：把对方要说的话小声递过去）；句意为舞台工作人员在侧幕给他提词，戏便接着演下去。

derivatives.zh: 由 prompt 加 -ly 构成，义为「迅速地；准时地」
由 prompt 加 -ness 构成，义为「迅速；及时」
由 prompt 加 -ing 构成，义为「提示；鼓励」
由 prompt 加 -er 构成，义为「提词员；提词器」

senses.title: Done quickly and without delay
senses.definition: acting or happening quickly, with no waiting in between
senses.definitionCN: 动作或事情发生得快，中间没有等待
senses.example: We received a prompt answer to our letter.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的信很快得到了答复。
senses.why: The Latin participle described something already brought out and therefore lying within reach, and what lies within reach can be used at once.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁分词描述的是已经被拿出来、因此就在手边的东西；就在手边的东西，随时都能用上。

senses.title: Arriving exactly at the agreed time
senses.definition: arriving or happening exactly at the stated time, neither early nor late
senses.definitionCN: 在约定的时刻到达或发生，不早也不晚
senses.example: Please be prompt for the eight o'clock train.
senses.exampleCN: 请准时赶上八点的火车。
senses.why: If readiness is the core, the clearest proof of readiness is being already there when the clock strikes, so the word takes on the sense of punctuality.
senses.whyCN: 如果核心是「随时可用」，那么最清楚的证明就是钟声一响人已经到位，于是这个词带上了「守时」的意思。

senses.title: To cause someone to do something
senses.definition: to make a person decide to do something, usually by something seen, heard or felt
senses.definitionCN: 通常因看到、听到或感到某事而使人决定去做
senses.example: The smell of smoke prompted him to check the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 烟味促使他去厨房查看。
senses.why: The verb first meant to bring words out of someone; from bringing out words it widened to bringing out any action at all.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词最初指把话从别人嘴里引出来；从「引出话」扩大到「引出任何行动」。

senses.title: To supply the next words to a speaker
senses.definition: to say the next words quietly to an actor or speaker who has forgotten them
senses.definitionCN: 小声把下一句台词说给忘词的演员或发言人
senses.example: The teacher prompted the child with the first word.
senses.exampleCN: 老师把第一个词提示给孩子。
senses.why: Theatre keeps the oldest visible sense: a helper at the side brings the forgotten line back into the actor's mouth.
senses.whyCN: 戏剧保留了最古老也最可见的那一层：助手在侧边把忘掉的台词重新送进演员嘴里。

senses.title: A cue or sign that tells you what to do next
senses.definition: a word, signal or symbol that shows a person, or a computer, what to do next
senses.definitionCN: 提示人或计算机下一步该做什么的词、信号或符号
senses.example: The program waits for a prompt before it continues.
senses.exampleCN: 程序会等一个提示符，然后才继续运行。
senses.why: A cue is still something brought out in front of you at the right moment, so the noun serves both the stage whisper and the blinking sign on a screen.
senses.whyCN: 提示仍然是在恰当的时刻被拿到你面前的东西，所以这个名词既能指舞台上的低语，也能指屏幕上闪动的记号。

intro.en: Prompt goes back to a Latin verb for taking something out; what has been brought out is ready at hand, and ready things act fast.
intro.cn: prompt 可追到拉丁语中表示「拿出来」的动词；被拿出来的东西就在手边，而在手边的东西动作就快。

items.en: Emere meant to take or to buy, the act of getting something into your hands.
items.cn: emere 意为拿取、购买，是把某物弄到手里的动作。

items.en: With pro-, the verb became promere, to bring forth or produce, as if drawing something out into the open.
items.cn: 加上 pro-，动词成为 promere，意为拿出来、取出，像是把东西从里面拿到明处。

items.en: The participle promptus described what had been brought forth, and so what was ready at hand and quick to use.
items.cn: 分词 promptus 描述已经被拿出来、因此就在手边、随时可用的东西。

items.en: Late Latin promptare meant to bring out or to suggest, and from it came the verb sense of urging someone to speak or act.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 promptare 意为拿出、提示，由它产生「催人开口或行动」的动词义。

items.en: French prompt entered English, which kept the adjective of readiness, added the verbs of urging and cueing, and later lent the noun to computing.
items.cn: 法语 prompt 进入英语，保留了「随时可用」的形容词义，加上「催促」与「提词」的动词义，后来又把名词借给了计算机领域。

note.en: The first group is the same Latin verb and the English forms built on it, including the phrase that still carries the old picture; the second group gathers words for speed and good timing.
note.cn: 第一组是同一拉丁动词及其上的英语形式，包括仍保留旧画面的那个说法；第二组收表示快与准时的词。

entries.definition: A person or device that supplies forgotten lines.
entries.definitionCN: 提示台词的人或设备；提词员、提词器。

entries.definition: The act of cueing someone, or a nudge that makes someone act.
entries.definitionCN: 给人提示的行为，或促使人行动的一推。

entries.definition: The quality of being quick and punctual.
entries.definitionCN: 迅速而准时的品质。

entries.definition: Done without preparation, literally done out of readiness.
entries.definitionCN: 即兴的、无准备的；字面义为「出自现成的状态」。

entries.definition: Moving or finishing in a short time.
entries.definitionCN: 在很短时间内移动或完成的。

entries.definition: Fast and smooth in movement, often in a literary tone.
entries.definitionCN: 动作又快又顺，常带文学色彩。

entries.definition: Happening at once, with nothing in between.
entries.definitionCN: 立刻发生，中间没有间隔。

entries.definition: Arriving exactly at the agreed time.
entries.definitionCN: 正好在约定的时间到达。

normalIntro.en: The whole family grows from one Latin picture: something is taken out and held ready, so it can be handed over the moment it is needed.
normalIntro.cn: 整族词都长自同一幅拉丁画面：东西被拿出来、握在手中待用，因此需要的那一刻就能递过去。

normal.en: Emere is to take, pro- is forward, so promere is to bring something out in front of you.
normal.cn: emere 是拿取，pro- 是向前，所以 promere 就是把东西拿到你面前。

normal.en: Promptus means already brought out, which explains why prompt means quick: ready things need no searching.
normal.cn: promptus 意为已经被拿出来，这就解释了 prompt 为什么是「快」：现成的东西不必再找。

normal.en: The verb sense of urging grows from the same image, because you bring words out of someone who has stopped speaking.
normal.cn: 动词「促使」也出自同一幅图：你把话从突然停住的人嘴里引出来。

normal.en: Impromptu keeps the Latin phrase in promptu, meaning in readiness, so an impromptu speech is one given straight out of what is at hand.
normal.cn: impromptu 保留了拉丁语 in promptu，意为「现成可用」，所以即兴演讲就是直接用手边现成的东西讲。

normal.en: A computer prompt is still a cue: the screen brings a question out and waits for your reply.
normal.cn: 计算机里的 prompt 仍是提示：屏幕把一个问题拿到你面前，然后等你的回答。

abstract.en: Prompt links speed to readiness, which suggests that haste here is not hurry but the absence of searching.
abstract.cn: prompt 把「快」和「现成」系在一起，说明这里的快不是慌忙，而是不必再找。

abstract.en: One word serves an actor's cue and a machine's signal, because both are a small push that keeps a process moving.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指演员的提词，也指机器的信号，因为两者都是让流程继续下去的一小推。

abstract.en: To prompt someone is to lend them the next step, and every prompt is therefore a small act of trust.
abstract.cn: 给人提示就是把下一步借给他，所以每次提示都是一次微小的信任。

examples.en: She gave a prompt reply to every question.
examples.cn: 她对每个问题都迅速作答。

examples.en: The letter prompted him to write back at once.
examples.cn: 这封信促使他立刻回信。

examples.en: The screen showed a prompt and waited.
examples.cn: 屏幕上出现一个提示，然后等着。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑荣扑」——有人在背后一推，人就扑腾着动起来；记住 prompt 是迅速的、促使人。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前、往外）+ emere（拿取、买）→ promere（拿出来、取出）→ promptus（已拿出来的、就在手边的）→ 晚期拉丁语 promptare（提示、催），经法语 prompt 进入英语；prompt 的「快」本义是「东西已在手边，随时可用」。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is something brought out and lying ready; from it come quickness, punctuality, the act of urging, the stage whisper and the screen cue.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「被拿出来、就在手边待用」；由此分出迅速、准时、促使人行动、舞台提词与屏幕提示。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand already holding what will be needed, so the moment it is asked for, it is there.
core.cn: 核心意象：手里早已握着待会儿要用的东西，别人一要，立刻就在。

branches.en: a reply handed over before it is even expected
branches.cn: 答复在别人预料之前就递到

branches.en: a smell of smoke sending someone to the kitchen
branches.cn: 烟味把人赶去厨房查看

branches.en: a whisper from the wings feeding the next line
branches.cn: 侧幕的低语把下一句递上台

branches.en: a blinking sign on a screen waiting for input
branches.cn: 屏幕上闪着的记号等着输入

branches.en: haste and cue living in one word
branches.cn: 迅速与提示共用一个词

intro.en: A Latin verb of taking out, its participle, and the English endings that make adverbs and nouns from the adjective hold the word together.
intro.cn: 表示「拿出来」的拉丁动词、它的分词，以及把这个形容词变成副词与名词的英语词尾，共同支撑这个词。

latinIntro.en: Promere and its participle promptus are the reliable Latin cognates, and emere is the verb inside promere.
latinIntro.cn: promere 及其分词 promptus 是可靠的同源词，而 emere 是 promere 里面的那个动词。

items.meaningCN: 已拿出来的；随时可用的

definition_zh: 营救；救援
definition_en: to save someone or something from danger or harm
core_image: 有人被水围住，救援者伸手把他拉上岸
scene: 洪水涨到窗台，消防员划着小船把一家人救了出来。 When the flood reached the windows, firefighters rescued the family in a small boat.
sceneCN: 这里 rescue 是「营救」（第 1 个义项：把某人从危险中救出）；句意：洪水涨到窗台时，消防员用一条小船把一家人救了出来。

derivatives.zh: 救援者
可营救的
未被救出的

senses.title: To save from immediate danger
senses.definition: to get someone out of a dangerous place or situation
senses.definitionCN: 把某人从危险的地方或处境中救出来
senses.example: Firefighters rescued two people from the burning house.
senses.exampleCN: 消防员从燃烧的房子里救出两个人。
senses.why: The word begins with people in danger, so the core sense is physical saving.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从身处危险的人开始，所以核心义是身体上的救助。

senses.title: To save from a difficult situation
senses.definition: to help someone or something escape failure or embarrassment
senses.definitionCN: 帮助某人或某物脱离失败或尴尬
senses.example: A last-minute goal rescued the team from defeat.
senses.exampleCN: 最后时刻的一个进球把球队从失败中挽救回来。
senses.why: The same pulling-out image is applied to failure rather than physical danger.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「拉出来」意象，被用在失败而非身体危险上。

senses.title: An act of saving
senses.definition: the act of saving someone from danger, or an operation that does so
senses.definitionCN: 把某人从危险中救出的行为，或为此展开的行动
senses.example: The rescue took place at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 营救行动在黎明时展开。
senses.why: The verb is also used as a noun for the whole operation.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词也作名词，指整个营救行动。

intro.en: Rescue comes from Old French rescourre, to shake off or set free, from Latin excutere, to shake out.
intro.cn: rescue 来自古法语 rescourre（抖脱、使自由），源于拉丁语 excutere（抖出）。

items.en: Quatere means to shake.
items.cn: quatere 意为摇动。

items.en: Excutere means to shake out or drive off.
items.cn: excutere 意为抖出、赶走。

items.en: Escourre means to shake off or free oneself.
items.cn: escourre 意为抖脱、脱身。

items.en: Rescourre means to set free from danger.
items.cn: rescourre 意为从危险中解救。

items.en: Middle English rescuen keeps the sense of saving from harm.
items.cn: 中古英语 rescuen 保留「使免于伤害」的意思。

items.en: Modern English uses rescue for danger, failure, and emergency operations.
items.cn: 现代英语中，rescue 用于危险、失败与紧急行动。

note.en: Rescue is a pulling-out word, and it sits near its own family and near verbs for saving and freeing.
note.cn: rescue 是一个「拉出来」的词，与自身词族以及表示拯救和释放的动词相邻。

entries.definition: a person who saves others from danger
entries.definitionCN: 救援者

entries.definition: able to be saved
entries.definitionCN: 可营救的

entries.definition: not yet saved
entries.definitionCN: 未被救出的

entries.definition: to keep someone safe from harm
entries.definitionCN: 救；保全

entries.definition: to release someone from being trapped
entries.definitionCN: 使自由；释放

entries.definition: to get something back after losing it
entries.definitionCN: 找回；收回

normalIntro.en: Rescue pictures a hand reaching into danger and pulling someone out.
normalIntro.cn: rescue 描绘一只手伸进危险，把人拉出来。

normal.en: The re- suggests pulling back, and the old root suggests shaking free.
normal.cn: re- 暗示往回拉，古老词根则暗示抖脱束缚。

normal.en: Rescue workers are the people who go in when others come out.
normal.cn: 救援人员就是别人往外跑时往里冲的人。

normal.en: Come to the rescue is a fixed phrase for offering help.
normal.cn: come to the rescue 是表示「前来帮忙」的固定短语。

normal.en: The noun and the verb look the same: a rescue, to rescue.
normal.cn: 名词和动词同形：a rescue 与 to rescue。

normal.en: Compare save: save is wider, while rescue usually means danger is present.
normal.cn: 对比 save：save 范围更广，rescue 通常意味着危险就在眼前。

abstract.en: Picture a rope thrown across dark water.
abstract.cn: 想象一条绳子被抛过漆黑的水面。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand gripping a wrist just before the current pulls.
abstract.cn: 想象在水流卷走前，一只手紧紧抓住手腕。

abstract.en: Think of a lighthouse beam finding a small boat.
abstract.cn: 想象灯塔的光束找到一条小船。

examples.en: Firefighters rescued two people from the burning house.
examples.cn: 消防员从燃烧的房子里救出两个人。

examples.en: A last-minute goal rescued the team from defeat.
examples.cn: 最后时刻的一个进球把球队从失败中挽救回来。

examples.en: The rescue took place at dawn.
examples.cn: 营救行动在黎明时展开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来救」——有危险时有人来救，就是 rescue；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 quatere（摇动）→ excutere（抖出）→ 古法语 escourre（抖脱）→ rescourre（解救）→ 中古英语 rescuen → 现代英语 rescue。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts with physical pulling out of danger, extends to rescue from failure, and also names the whole operation.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从把身体从危险中拉出开始，扩展到从失败中挽救，也可指整个营救行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching into danger and pulling someone to safety.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手伸进危险，把人拉到安全处。

branches.en: Saving from physical danger is the core sense.
branches.cn: 从身体危险中救人，是核心义项。

branches.en: Saving from failure applies the pull to reputation or chances.
branches.cn: 从失败中挽救，把「拉」用于声誉或机会。

branches.en: The noun names the whole saving operation.
branches.cn: 名词指整个营救行动。

branches.en: Physical and figurative rescues both end in relief.
branches.cn: 身体与比喻意义上的营救都以松一口气结束。

branches.en: The act and the operation are described by the same word.
branches.cn: 救助行为与救援行动用同一个词描述。

intro.en: Rescue is a French verb built on a Latin root for shaking, with English endings forming its small family.
intro.cn: rescue 是建立在拉丁语「摇动」词根上的法语动词，小词族由英语词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin quatere means to shake, and excutere means to shake out or drive off.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 quatere 意为摇动，excutere 意为抖出或赶走。

items.exampleCN: re- 增添「往回拉」的意思。

items.example: Excutere gives the idea of shaking free.
Escourre carries the verb into French.
items.exampleCN: escourre 把这个动词带入法语。

items.example: Rescourre is the direct source of rescue.
items.exampleCN: rescourre 是 rescue 的直接来源。

definition_zh: 罪孽；罪恶；过失
definition_en: an act that breaks a religious or moral law
core_image: 教堂里低垂的烛火与忏悔的人影
scene: 在许多宗教里，偷窃被视为罪孽。 In many religions, stealing is considered a sin.
sceneCN: 这里 sin 是「罪孽」（第 1 个义项）；句意：在许多宗教里，偷窃被视为罪孽。

derivatives.zh: 有罪的
罪人
无罪的

senses.title: A wrong against religious law
senses.definition: an act that breaks a law of God or a religion
senses.definitionCN: 违反上帝或宗教律法的行为
senses.example: In many religions, stealing is considered a sin.
senses.exampleCN: 在许多宗教里，偷窃被视为罪孽。
senses.why: This is the oldest and strongest sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老也最强烈的义项。

senses.title: A serious moral wrong
senses.definition: a very bad act in moral terms
senses.definitionCN: 道德意义上非常恶劣的行为
senses.example: Cruelty to children is a sin no law can excuse.
senses.exampleCN: 虐待儿童是任何法律都无法开脱的罪恶。
senses.why: The religious word widened into moral judgment.
senses.whyCN: 宗教用语扩展为道德评判。

senses.title: A small fault
senses.definition: a minor fault or mistake
senses.definitionCN: 轻微的过错或失误
senses.example: He treats every mistake as a sin.
senses.exampleCN: 他把每一个错误都当成过失。
senses.why: In casual use the word can sound gentle.
senses.whyCN: 在口语中这个词也可以显得轻微。

intro.en: Sin is one of the oldest moral words in English.
intro.cn: sin 是英语中最古老的道德词汇之一。

items.en: Synn meant wrong doing.
items.cn: synn 意为做错事。

items.en: Syngian was the verb to sin.
items.cn: syngian 是表示犯罪的动词。

items.en: The spelling became sinne.
items.cn: 拼写变为 sinne。

items.en: The modern form is sin.
items.cn: 现代词形是 sin。

items.en: It also covers small everyday faults.
items.cn: 它也兼指日常生活里的小过失。

note.en: Sin is compared with similar-looking words and words for wrong.
note.cn: 把 sin 与形近词以及表示过错的词作比较。

entries.definition: a mathematical ratio
entries.definitionCN: 正弦

entries.definition: a male child
entries.definitionCN: 儿子

entries.definition: the star that gives light
entries.definitionCN: 太阳

entries.definition: an unjust act
entries.definitionCN: 错误；不义

entries.definition: great wickedness
entries.definitionCN: 邪恶

entries.definition: an act against the law
entries.definitionCN: 罪行

normalIntro.en: Sin names a wrong that is judged by faith or conscience.
normalIntro.cn: sin 指由信仰或良心来评判的过错。

normal.en: In many religions, stealing is considered a sin.
normal.cn: 在许多宗教里，偷窃被视为罪孽。

normal.en: Cruelty to children is a sin no law can excuse.
normal.cn: 虐待儿童是任何法律都无法开脱的罪恶。

normal.en: He treats every mistake as a sin.
normal.cn: 他把每一个错误都当成过失。

normal.en: She confessed her sins in the quiet church.
normal.cn: 她在安静的教堂里忏悔自己的罪过。

normal.en: To tell a lie is not always a sin.
normal.cn: 说谎未必总是罪过。

abstract.en: A sin is a line crossed in the heart.
abstract.cn: 罪孽是心里越过的一条线。

abstract.en: Guilt is the echo of a sin.
abstract.cn: 内疚是罪过的回声。

abstract.en: Mercy speaks to the one who has sinned.
abstract.cn: 慈悲是对犯过罪的人说话。

examples.en: In many religions, stealing is considered a sin.
examples.cn: 在许多宗教里，偷窃被视为罪孽。

examples.en: She confessed her sins in the quiet church.
examples.cn: 她在安静的教堂里忏悔自己的罪过。

examples.en: Cruelty to children is a sin no law can excuse.
examples.cn: 虐待儿童是任何法律都无法开脱的罪恶。

dict_mnemonic.text: sin 与 son、sun 形近音近，但意思完全不同；记住教堂里的「罪孽」画面，就不会混淆。

root: 源自古英语 synn（做错事），核心义「违背信仰或良心的过错」。

sensesIntro.en: Sin means a wrong against religious law, a serious moral wrong, or a small fault.
sensesIntro.cn: sin 意为违背宗教律法的罪孽、道德上的罪恶或小过失。

core.en: A wrong judged by faith and conscience.
core.cn: 由信仰与良心评判的过错。

branches.en: A believer names stealing a sin.
branches.cn: 信徒把偷窃称为罪孽。

branches.en: Cruelty shocks the conscience.
branches.cn: 残忍震撼了良心。

branches.en: A small mistake is called a sin in jest.
branches.cn: 小错在玩笑中也被称为过失。

branches.en: Faith and conscience both say no to the act.
branches.cn: 信仰和良心都对该行为说不。

branches.en: The same word covers a grave wrong and a small fault.
branches.cn: 同一个词既指重罪，也指小过。

intro.en: Sin builds words for guilt, wrongdoers, and innocence.
intro.cn: sin 构成表示罪责、罪人和无罪的词。

latinIntro.en: Sin is an Old English word, not from Latin.
latinIntro.cn: sin 是古英语词，并非来自拉丁语。

items.example: He would not commit a sin.

items.exampleCN: 这个故事列举了他的罪过。
传道人欢迎每一个罪人。

items.example: He refused to commit a sin.

definition_zh: 乏味的；迟钝的；暗淡的；沉闷的；（疼痛）隐约的；（刀）钝的
definition_en: not interesting, slow to understand, not bright or sharp, not clear as a pain is not sharp, or to make something less sharp or lively
core_image: 一把卷了刃的旧刀，切不开纸，也照不出光
scene: 讲座在昏暗的灯下进行，前排已有人开始打瞌睡。 The lecture was accurate but dull.
sceneCN: 这里 dull 是「乏味的」（第 1 个义项：没有趣味、让人提不起精神）；句意是那场讲座虽然准确，却很乏味。

pos.zh: 形容词：乏味的；迟钝的；暗淡的；钝的
动词：使迟钝；使减弱；使变暗

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「乏味；迟钝；暗淡」
由本词加表人后缀 -ard 构成，义为「迟钝的人；笨人」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「乏味地；迟钝地；暗淡地」

senses.title: Not interesting
senses.definition: lacking interest, excitement or variety, so that it is hard to pay attention
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏趣味、刺激或变化，使人难以集中注意
senses.example: The lecture was accurate but dull.
senses.exampleCN: 那场讲座虽然准确，却很乏味。
senses.why: A dull blade cannot cut, and a dull event cannot hold attention; the same word marks an edge that has lost its bite.
senses.whyCN: 钝刀切不动东西，乏味的事抓不住注意力；同一个词都在标记一把失去锋刃的「刃」。

senses.title: Not sharp, as a blade
senses.definition: having an edge that is not sharp and therefore cuts poorly
senses.definitionCN: 刃口不锋利，因此切割效果差
senses.example: The knife was too dull to cut the bread.
senses.exampleCN: 那把刀太钝，切不开面包。
senses.why: This is the physical source: a dull edge reflects no light along its line and does not part what it touches.
senses.whyCN: 这是物理源头：钝刃沿刃线反不出光，也分不开它所接触的东西。

senses.title: Slow to understand
senses.definition: slow to learn, notice or understand things
senses.definitionCN: 学习、察觉或理解事物较慢
senses.example: The drugs had left his mind dull for a few hours.
senses.exampleCN: 那些药让他的头脑迟钝了几个小时。
senses.why: A mind without a sharp edge is pictured like a blade without one: it still works, but it no longer cuts quickly.
senses.whyCN: 没有锋刃的头脑被比作没有刃口的刀：还能用，却不再切得快。

senses.title: Not bright or clear
senses.definition: not bright, not shiny and not clear, as light, colour or weather
senses.definitionCN: 不明亮、不反光、不清晰，如光线、颜色或天气
senses.example: The sky turned a dull grey before the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨前，天空变成暗淡的灰色。
senses.why: Light on a dull surface scatters instead of shining back, so the word moves easily from metal to sky and paint.
senses.whyCN: 光落在暗淡的表面上会散开而不是反射回来，所以这个词很容易从金属移到天空和油漆。

senses.title: Faint, as pain
senses.definition: felt as a steady but not sharp pain, more aching than stabbing
senses.definitionCN: 持续的、不尖锐的疼痛，更像酸痛而非刺痛
senses.example: She felt a dull ache in her shoulder.
senses.exampleCN: 她感到肩膀有一阵隐隐的酸痛。
senses.why: Pain with no sharp point is like a blade with no edge: present and heavy, but not cutting.
senses.whyCN: 没有尖锐痛点的疼，就像没有刃口的刀：存在且沉重，却不切割。

senses.title: To make less sharp
senses.definition: to make something less sharp, bright, strong or interesting
senses.definitionCN: 使某物变得不那么锋利、明亮、强烈或有趣
senses.example: The medicine dulled the pain within an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 药物在一小时内减轻了疼痛。
senses.why: The verb applies the adjective to an object: it removes the edge, the shine or the intensity.
senses.whyCN: 动词把形容词施加到某物上：去掉它的锋刃、光泽或强度。

intro.en: Dull is a native English adjective whose earliest recorded senses are slow and stupid; the physical sense of a blunt edge came alongside.
intro.cn: dull 是本族语英语形容词，最早记录的义项是「迟钝、愚笨」，钝刃这一物理义同时并存。

items.en: A root connected with slowness or foolishness is sometimes suggested, but its exact form and deeper origin are uncertain.
items.cn: 有人提出它与表示「迟缓、愚笨」的词根有关，但其确切形式和更早来源不确定。

items.en: Old English dol meant foolish or slow-witted and is a likely relative rather than a direct ancestor.
items.cn: 古英语 dol 意为「愚笨、迟钝」，很可能是亲属词而非直系祖先。

items.en: Middle English dul spread from people to edges, colours and weather, where sharpness or brightness was missing.
items.cn: 中古英语 dul 从人扩展到刃口、颜色和天气，指缺少锋利或明亮。

items.en: The senses of a blunt blade and a dim surface are recorded by the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 钝刃与暗淡表面这两个义项在十四世纪已有记录。

items.en: The figurative sense of boring speech grew from the image of an edge that no longer cuts.
items.cn: 言语乏味的比喻义，是从「刃口不再切割」这一意象生长出来的。

items.en: Dull pain, dull weather and dull the pain show the word applied to sensation and to relief.
items.cn: dull pain、dull weather 与 dull the pain 展示了这个词用在感觉与缓解上。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on dull; the near-meaning group separates boring, blunt and dim, which cover different missing qualities.
note.cn: 形近组收由 dull 构成的词形；近义组区分 boring、blunt 与 dim，它们各自缺少的品质不同。

entries.definition: The state of being dull in any of its senses; dull plus -ness.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指乏味、迟钝或暗淡的状态，由 dull 加 -ness 构成。

entries.definition: A slow or stupid person; dull plus the person suffix -ard.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指迟钝或愚笨的人，由 dull 加表人后缀 -ard 构成。

entries.definition: In a dull manner, without brightness, sharpness or interest.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「乏味地、迟钝地、暗淡地」。

entries.definition: Having eyes that show no interest or brightness; dull plus eyed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「目光呆滞的」，由 dull 与 eyed 复合。

entries.definition: Making someone feel tired and uninterested; more direct and personal than dull.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人厌烦的」，比 dull 更直接、更针对人的感受。

entries.definition: Having a thick edge that does not cut well; the physical twin of dull.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「钝的」，是 dull 物理义的同义词。

entries.definition: Not bright, as light or colour; it covers the brightness sense only.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「昏暗的」，只覆盖明亮度这一义项。

entries.definition: Moving or responding more slowly than normal; it describes pace, not interest.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「迟缓的」，描述速度而非趣味。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the image of a blunt edge and follow it into minds, weather and pain.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子守住「钝刃」这一意象，再跟着它走进头脑、天气与疼痛。

normal.en: A dull knife cannot cut; start there and every other sense makes sense.
normal.cn: 钝刀切不动，从这里出发，其他义项都说得通。

normal.en: A dull mind is a blade without an edge: still there, but slow to cut.
normal.cn: 迟钝的头脑就是没有刃口的刀：还在，却切得慢。

normal.en: A dull sky gives no shine, and a dull grey wall gives none either.
normal.cn: 阴沉的天空没有光泽，暗淡的灰墙也没有。

normal.en: A dull ache is pain with no point, like a blade with no edge.
normal.cn: 隐隐的酸痛是没有尖端的疼，就像没有刃口的刀。

normal.en: To dull the pain is to take the edge off it, the same image as a verb.
normal.cn: to dull the pain 就是把疼痛的锋刃去掉，还是同一个意象。

abstract.en: Picture a blade lying on a table, its edge rounded by years of use.
abstract.cn: 想象一把刀躺在桌上，刃口被多年使用磨圆了。

abstract.en: Draw the same rounded line across a page of prose and a grey afternoon sky.
abstract.cn: 把同一条磨圆的线画在一页文字上，也画在一个灰色的午后天空上。

abstract.en: Dull is always a missing edge: in metal, in light, in wit or in pain.
abstract.cn: dull 永远是一种缺失的锋刃：在金属里、在光里、在机敏里，或在疼痛里。

examples.en: The lecture was accurate but dull.
examples.cn: 那场讲座虽然准确，却很乏味。

examples.en: The knife was too dull to cut the bread.
examples.cn: 那把刀太钝，切不开面包。

examples.en: The medicine dulled the pain within an hour.
examples.cn: 药物在一小时内减轻了疼痛。

dict_mnemonic.text: dull 是一把卷了刃的刀：刀钝了，光暗了，人反应慢了，话也就乏味了。

root: 本族语英语形容词，最早义项为「迟钝、愚笨」，与古英语 dol 可能是亲属关系；中古英语 dul 扩展到钝刃、暗淡的颜色与阴沉的天气。更早的印欧语来源一般与「迟缓」相关，确切形式不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses of dull all describe a missing edge: in a blade, in light, in a mind, in interest, in pain, or in the act of removing sharpness.
sensesIntro.cn: dull 的六个义项都在描述一种缺失的锋刃：在刀刃上、在光里、在头脑里、在趣味里、在疼痛里，或在去掉锋刃的动作里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old knife with a rounded edge that neither cuts nor shines.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把刃口磨圆的旧刀，既切不动也不反光。

branches.en: THE EDGE: the physical blade that no longer parts what it touches.
branches.cn: 刃口线：物理上的刀刃不再分开它接触的东西。

branches.en: THE LIGHT: a surface that scatters light instead of shining back.
branches.cn: 光线线：表面把光散开，而不是反射回来。

branches.en: THE MIND: a person who still thinks but no longer cuts quickly.
branches.cn: 头脑线：人还能思考，却不再反应迅速。

branches.en: THE PAGE: speech or writing with no edge to hold attention.
branches.cn: 书页线：言谈或文字没有能抓住注意力的锋刃。

branches.en: THE BODY: a pain without a point, and the act of taking that point away.
branches.cn: 身体线：没有尖端的疼痛，以及把尖端去掉的动作。

intro.en: Dull is a native adjective; English adds -ness, -ard, -ly, -ed and -ing to build its family.
intro.cn: dull 是本族语形容词；英语加 -ness、-ard、-ly、-ed、-ing 来扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor; Latin hebes, blunt or dull, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语祖先；拉丁语 hebes（钝的、迟钝的）只是语义对照。

items.example: The adjective is the base of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是词族的基础。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「乏味；迟钝；暗淡」
由本词加表人后缀 -ard 构成，义为「迟钝的人；笨人」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「乏味地；迟钝地；暗淡地」

definition_zh: 力量；实力；强度
definition_en: the physical power of a body, a strong quality, or the degree to which something can resist force
core_image: 一个人绷紧手臂，把重物稳稳举过头顶
scene: 他需要力气才能搬动那块石头。 He needed strength to move the stone.
sceneCN: 这里 strength 是「力量」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他需要力气才能搬动那块石头。

derivatives.zh: 强壮的；强的
加强；巩固
强有力地

senses.title: Physical power
senses.definition: the physical power of a person or animal
senses.definitionCN: 人或动物身体的力量
senses.example: He needed strength to move the stone.
senses.exampleCN: 他需要力气才能搬动那块石头。
senses.why: This is power in the muscles.
senses.whyCN: 这是肌肉里的力量。

senses.title: A strong point
senses.definition: a quality or ability in which someone is strong
senses.definitionCN: 某人擅长的地方或优势
senses.example: Patience is her greatest strength.
senses.exampleCN: 耐心是她最大的长处。
senses.why: Power can also live in character.
senses.whyCN: 力量也可以存在于品格之中。

senses.title: Resistance to force
senses.definition: how well a material or argument holds up
senses.definitionCN: 材料或论点承受压力的程度
senses.example: Engineers tested the strength of the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师测试了这座桥的强度。
senses.why: The idea of power moves into objects.
senses.whyCN: 力量的概念被移到了物体上。

intro.en: Strength comes from Old English strengþu, physical power.
intro.cn: strength 来自古英语 strengþu，意为身体的力量。

items.en: Strengþu meant bodily power.
items.cn: strengþu 指身体的力量。

items.en: It shared a root with strong.
items.cn: 它与 strong 共用一个词根。

items.en: Strengthe kept the sense of might.
items.cn: 中古英语 strengthe 仍指力量。

items.en: Strength also named a person's good quality.
items.cn: strength 也开始指人的长处。

items.en: It came to measure materials and arguments.
items.cn: 它又被用来衡量材料与论点的强度。

note.en: Strength is compared with look-alike words and with words for power.
note.cn: 把 strength 与形近词以及表示力量的词作比较。

entries.definition: the measure from end to end
entries.definitionCN: 长度

entries.definition: to make stronger
entries.definitionCN: 加强

entries.definition: unusual
entries.definitionCN: 奇怪的

entries.definition: the ability to act or control
entries.definitionCN: 力量；权力

entries.definition: physical energy or violence
entries.definitionCN: 力；武力

entries.definition: great power
entries.definitionCN: 强大力量

normalIntro.en: Strength is power in muscle, in character, and in stone.
normalIntro.cn: strength 是肌肉里的力量、品格里的力量，也是石头里的力量。

normal.en: He lifted the box with great strength.
normal.cn: 他用很大的力气抬起箱子。

normal.en: She found inner strength in hard times.
normal.cn: 艰难时她找到了内心的力量。

normal.en: The team is back at full strength.
normal.cn: 队伍恢复了全部实力。

normal.en: Honesty is one of his strengths.
normal.cn: 诚实是他的长处之一。

normal.en: The wall has great strength.
normal.cn: 这堵墙非常坚固。

abstract.en: Strength is the quiet behind a steady hand.
abstract.cn: 力量，是稳稳的手背后那份安静。

abstract.en: Some strength is only found when it is needed.
abstract.cn: 有些力量，只有在需要时才被找到。

abstract.en: Stone strength is patience under weight.
abstract.cn: 石头的强度，是承重时的耐心。

examples.en: He needed strength to move the stone.
examples.cn: 他需要力气才能搬动那块石头。

examples.en: Patience is her greatest strength.
examples.cn: 耐心是她最大的长处。

examples.en: Engineers tested the strength of the bridge.
examples.cn: 工程师测试了这座桥的强度。

dict_mnemonic.text: strength 是 strong 的名词；肌肉里的力量是力气，人擅长的地方是长处，材料扛得住是强度。

root: 来自古英语 strengþu（力量），与 strong 同源；由身体的力量，引申为人的长处与优势，再用于材料、论点等可承受压力的程度。

sensesIntro.en: Strength is muscle power, a personal strong point, and the power of a thing to resist force.
sensesIntro.cn: strength 是肌肉的力量、个人的长处，以及物体抵抗外力的能力。

core.en: A heavy stone held steady above the head.
core.cn: 一块重石被稳稳举过头顶。

branches.en: Arms tighten and the load rises.
branches.cn: 手臂收紧，重物升起。

branches.en: A calm word wins a hard day.
branches.cn: 一句平静的话撑过艰难的一天。

branches.en: A bridge holds in the wind.
branches.cn: 桥在风中屹立不动。

branches.en: What the body learns, the character keeps.
branches.cn: 身体学会的，品格会留下。

branches.en: A strong argument and a strong beam both resist pressure.
branches.cn: 有力的论点和坚固的梁，都扛得住压力。

intro.en: Strength forms a plural and connects to strong and strengthen.
intro.cn: strength 有复数，并与 strong、strengthen 相连。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.example: The team played at full strength.

definition_zh: 果酱；堵塞；拥挤；卡住；（无线电）干扰；塞满
definition_en: a sweet food made by boiling fruit with sugar, a crowd or blockage that stops movement, or to press something tightly into a space
core_image: 狭窄的巷口被一群人挤得水泄不通，谁也动不了
scene: 早高峰的路口，两侧的车都往前挤，最后谁都不动。 The morning traffic jam stretched for two kilometres.
sceneCN: 这里 jam 是「堵塞」（第 1 个义项：人和车挤在一起无法移动），句意为早高峰的堵车队伍排了两公里。画面里的物件：路口、车流、红灯。

pos.zh: 名词：果酱；堵塞；拥挤；困境

derivatives.zh: 由过去分词转形容词，义为「卡住的；挤满的」
由 jam 加 -ing 构成，义为「干扰；即兴合奏」
由 jam 加 -y 构成，义为「涂果酱的；幸运的」

senses.title: A blockage of traffic
senses.definition: a line of vehicles or people so crowded that they cannot move
senses.definitionCN: 车辆或人群挤到无法移动
senses.example: A jam at the bridge delayed every bus.
senses.exampleCN: 桥上的堵车让所有公交都晚了。
senses.why: The verb meant to press tightly, and a jam is the result of pressing a road full.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词本义是紧紧压住，堵塞就是把路压满的结果。

senses.title: A tight press of people
senses.definition: a crowd of people or things squeezed into a space too small for them
senses.definitionCN: 拥挤到超过空间容量的人群或物体
senses.example: There was a jam of fans at the stage door.
senses.exampleCN: 后台门口挤着一堆粉丝。
senses.why: Crowding is the same pressing action applied to people instead of vehicles.
senses.whyCN: 拥挤就是把「压」的动作用于人而不是车。

senses.title: Fruit boiled with sugar
senses.definition: a thick sweet spread made by boiling fruit with sugar
senses.definitionCN: 水果加糖煮成的浓稠甜酱
senses.example: She spread jam on the toast.
senses.exampleCN: 她在吐司上抹了果酱。
senses.why: The food sense has a different origin, likely from crushing fruit, but the word fused.
senses.whyCN: 食物义的来源不同，可能取自「压碎水果」，但词形融合在了一起。

senses.title: To squeeze into a space
senses.definition: to push something into a place with force so that it fits tightly
senses.definitionCN: 用力把东西推进某处使之紧紧塞住
senses.example: He jammed the clothes into the small case.
senses.exampleCN: 他把衣服硬塞进那只小箱子。
senses.why: This is the central physical sense: force something in until there is no play left.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心的物理义：硬推进去直到不留余量。

senses.title: To be stuck
senses.definition: to become unable to move or work because a part is stuck
senses.definitionCN: 因部件卡住而不能移动或运转
senses.example: The printer jammed again in the night.
senses.exampleCN: 打印机夜里又卡纸了。
senses.why: Something jammed has been pressed until its parts cannot slide.
senses.whyCN: jam 住的东西被压到各部件无法滑动。

senses.title: To block a signal
senses.definition: to send out signals that stop a radio or other transmission being received
senses.definitionCN: 发出信号使电台等无法被接收
senses.example: Electronic noise jammed the radio in the tunnel.
senses.exampleCN: 电子噪声干扰了隧道里的收音机。
senses.why: Jamming fills a channel with noise the way a crowd fills a street.
senses.whyCN: 干扰就像人群填满街一样，把一条频道填满噪声。

intro.en: Jam in the sense of squeezing may echo a French dialect verb for pressing, while the fruit sense probably grows from crushing fruit; the exact path is debated.
intro.cn: 表示「挤压」的 jam 可能源自法语方言里「压」的动词，果酱义大概出自「把水果压碎」，具体路径仍有争议。

items.en: A dialect verb for pressing or squeezing sits behind the English verb.
items.cn: 英语动词背后可能有一个表示「压、挤」的法语方言动词。

items.en: English dialects used jam for squeezing or bruising fruit.
items.cn: 英语方言里 jam 指压挤、压伤水果。

items.en: The noun for a crowd or blocked street appears in the early nineteenth century records.
items.cn: 表示人群拥挤或街道堵塞的名词在十九世纪初见于记录。

items.en: jam as fruit boiled with sugar is recorded from the eighteenth century and spread in the next.
items.cn: 果酱义在十八世纪已有记录，之后普及。

items.en: Radio jamming joined the family in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 无线电干扰义在二十世纪加入这一词族。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the jam- shape; the near-meaning group holds words for jams, crowds, and squeezing.
note.cn: 形近组共用 jam- 词形；近义组收堵塞、拥挤与挤压类词。

entries.definition: Stuck or packed tight.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「卡住的；挤满的」。

entries.definition: Blocking signals, or playing music freely.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「干扰；即兴合奏」。

entries.definition: Covered with jam, or very lucky.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加 -y 构成，义为「抹了果酱的；幸好运的」。

entries.definition: To stop movement through a passage.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「阻挡」，比 jam 更强调阻止。

entries.definition: A large number of people in one place.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「人群」，只指人多。

entries.definition: To press something firmly from two sides.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「挤压」，力度更轻。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the physical squeeze as the centre and hang traffic, fruit, and jammed printers on it.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把「硬压」这个物理动作放在中心，再挂上堵车、果酱与卡纸的打印机。

normal.en: To jam is to press something in until no gap is left.
normal.cn: jam 就是压进去直到不留缝。

normal.en: A traffic jam is a street pressed full of cars.
normal.cn: traffic jam 就是被车压满的街。

normal.en: Jam is fruit pressed and boiled with sugar.
normal.cn: jam 是压碎加糖煮的水果。

normal.en: A printer that jams has paper stuck inside.
normal.cn: 卡住的打印机里面有纸塞着。

normal.en: Jamming a radio fills its channel with noise.
normal.cn: 干扰收音机就是拿噪声填满频道。

abstract.en: A jam is a space that has lost all its gaps.
abstract.cn: 堵塞是失去全部缝隙的一处空间。

abstract.en: Everyone pushing forward is what stops everyone.
abstract.cn: 人人向前挤，正是人人不能动的原因。

abstract.en: Sweet jam begins with crushing hard fruit.
abstract.cn: 甜的果酱从压碎硬水果开始。

examples.en: We were stuck in a jam for forty minutes.
examples.cn: 我们堵在路上四十分钟。

examples.en: He jammed the papers into the drawer and left.
examples.cn: 他把文件塞进抽屉就走了。

examples.en: Pass me the jam, please.
examples.cn: 请把果酱递给我。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扎满」—— 人车扎得满满，一点空隙都没有

root: 源自法语／英语方言表示「压、挤」的动词 → 英语 jam「挤压」→ 拥挤、堵塞、卡住、果酱、干扰。同族有 jammed、jamming、traffic jam。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses: traffic blockage, a crowd, fruit jam, squeezing something in, being stuck, and signal interference.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项：交通堵塞、人群拥挤、果酱、把东西塞满、卡住，以及信号干扰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow lane packed so tight that nobody can move.
core.cn: 核心意象：狭窄的巷口被挤得谁也动不了。

branches.en: THE BRIDGE: cars nose to nose for two kilometres.
branches.cn: 桥这条线：两公里的车首尾相接。

branches.en: THE DOOR: fans pressed against a stage entrance.
branches.cn: 门口这条线：粉丝挤在后台门前。

branches.en: THE TOAST: crushed fruit turned sweet and thick.
branches.cn: 吐司这条线：压碎的果子变甜变稠。

branches.en: THE CASE AND THE PRINTER: pushed in until stuck.
branches.cn: 箱子与打印机这条线：推到卡住为止。

branches.en: THE TUNNEL: noise filling a radio channel.
branches.cn: 隧道这条线：噪声填满收音频道。

intro.en: Jam is a short English word with no classical prefix; its endings are all English.
intro.cn: jam 是简短的英语词，没有古典词缀，所有词尾都是英语的。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for jam, so latinEntries is empty; the dotted form jam. shows the word is a whole noun.
latinIntro.cn: jam 没有拉丁语来源，latinEntries 留空；带点的 jam. 表示它是一个完整名词。

items.example: The central meaning of the word.
Dictionaries write jam. to show sense number.
items.exampleCN: 词典用 jam. 来标出义项序号。

definition_zh: 完全地；彻底地；仅仅
definition_en: completely, or only and nothing else
core_image: 一块布从头铺到尾，没有一寸遗漏
scene: 暴雨过后，整条山路都被泥水覆盖。 After the storm, mud covered the mountain path entirely.
sceneCN: 这里 entirely 是「完全地」（第 1 个义项：在程度或范围上毫无遗漏）；句意：暴雨过后，泥水把山路完全盖住了。

derivatives.zh: 全部的；完整的
整体；全部
完整性

senses.title: Completely, in every part
senses.definition: in every part or to the full degree, with nothing missing
senses.definitionCN: 在每一部分上或达到十足程度，没有任何遗漏
senses.example: I agree with you entirely.
senses.exampleCN: 我完全同意你。
senses.why: The adverb adds -ly to entire, so it describes something done in a whole and complete way.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词由 entire 加 -ly 构成，所以描述以完整、彻底的方式完成某事。

senses.title: Solely, and nothing else
senses.definition: used to say that something is only or wholly due to one thing
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示某事仅仅或完全由于某一原因
senses.example: The decision was entirely hers.
senses.exampleCN: 这个决定完全是她做的。
senses.why: If something is whole, nothing else is mixed in, so entirely can mean solely.
senses.whyCN: 如果某物是完整的，就没有别的东西掺入，因此 entirely 可以表示「仅仅」。

senses.title: Fully and without reservation
senses.definition: with complete commitment or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 带着完全的投入或赞同
senses.example: She trusted him entirely.
senses.exampleCN: 她完全信任他。
senses.why: Complete agreement leaves no room for doubt, which gives the sense of full-hearted trust.
senses.whyCN: 完全的赞同不留怀疑余地，于是产生「全心信任」的含义。

intro.en: Entirely is the adverb of entire, which comes from Latin integer, whole and untouched, through Old French entier.
intro.cn: entirely 是 entire 的副词形式；entire 来自拉丁语 integer（完整、未被触碰），经古法语 entier 进入英语。

items.en: Tangere means to touch or handle.
items.cn: tangere 意为触碰或接触。

items.en: In- here means not.
items.cn: 这里的 in- 表示「不」。

items.en: Integer means whole and untouched.
items.cn: integer 意为完整的、未被触碰的。

items.en: Entier keeps the sense of whole and complete.
items.cn: entier 保留「完整、完全」的意思。

items.en: Entire describes something whole and sound.
items.cn: 中古英语 entire 描述完整而完好之物。

items.en: The adverb entirely means completely or solely.
items.cn: 现代英语副词 entirely 表示完全地或仅仅。

note.en: Entirely belongs to the entire family and sits close to adverbs for complete degree.
note.cn: entirely 属于 entire 词族，并与表示完全程度的副词相邻。

entries.definition: whole, with no part missing
entries.definitionCN: 全部的；完整的

entries.definition: the state of being whole
entries.definitionCN: 整体；全部

entries.definition: completeness
entries.definitionCN: 完整性

entries.definition: in every way
entries.definitionCN: 完全地；彻底地

entries.definition: entirely, without exception
entries.definitionCN: 完全地；全部地

entries.definition: completely and only
entries.definitionCN: 完全地；纯粹地

normalIntro.en: Entirely is simply entire plus -ly: whatever is whole is done in a whole way.
normalIntro.cn: entirely 就是 entire 加 -ly：完整的东西，就以完整的方式去做。

normal.en: Entire means whole, so entirely means in a whole way.
normal.cn: entire 意为完整，所以 entirely 表示以完整的方式。

normal.en: Not entirely sure means not completely sure.
normal.cn: not entirely sure 就是不完全确定。

normal.en: The phrase entirely up to you means completely your choice.
normal.cn: 短语 entirely up to you 表示完全由你决定。

normal.en: Entirely can also mean solely, as in entirely her fault.
normal.cn: entirely 也可表示「仅仅」，如 entirely her fault。

normal.en: Compare partly, its opposite in degree.
normal.cn: 对比 partly，它是程度上的反义词。

abstract.en: Picture a blank sheet with no edge torn.
abstract.cn: 想象一张空白纸，边缘一处也没有撕破。

abstract.en: Imagine a lamp lighting every corner of one room.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯照亮一个房间的每个角落。

abstract.en: Think of a full glass filled to the very brim.
abstract.cn: 想象一只玻璃杯被倒到最满。

examples.en: The room was entirely empty when we arrived.
examples.cn: 我们到达时，房间完全是空的。

examples.en: Her answer was not entirely honest.
examples.cn: 她的回答并不完全诚实。

examples.en: The program is entirely free for students.
examples.cn: 这个项目对学生完全免费。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「in + tire」——轮胎一个都没落下，整辆车都齐全；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）＋ tangere（触碰）→ integer（完整无缺）→ 古法语 entier → entire ＋ -ly → entirely，核心义「完整地、完全地」。

sensesIntro.en: Entirely first means in every part, then narrows to solely, and finally describes full-hearted commitment.
sensesIntro.cn: entirely 先表示在每一部分上，再收窄为「仅仅」，最后描述毫无保留的投入。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole sheet spread out with no corner missing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整块布铺开，没有缺角。

branches.en: Completeness in every part is the main adverbial sense.
branches.cn: 每一部分都完整，是主要副词义项。

branches.en: Wholeness with nothing mixed in gives the sense of solely.
branches.cn: 完整而没有别物掺入，产生「仅仅」的含义。

branches.en: Complete agreement extends the idea to full trust.
branches.cn: 完全的赞同把这一概念扩展到全心信任。

branches.en: Doing something completely often means doing it wholeheartedly.
branches.cn: 完全地做某事，往往意味着全身心投入。

branches.en: A decision made solely by one person can be trusted entirely.
branches.cn: 完全由一个人做出的决定，也可以被完全信任。

intro.en: Entirely is a Latin adjective reshaped by French, with the English adverb suffix -ly.
intro.cn: entirely 是经法语改造的拉丁形容词，加上英语副词词尾 -ly。

latinIntro.en: Latin integer means whole or untouched, from in-, not, and tangere, to touch.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 integer 意为完整或未被触碰，由 in-（不）与 tangere（触碰）构成。

items.example: Tangere supplies the idea of touch.

items.example: Entier carries the word into French.
items.exampleCN: entier 把这个词带入法语。
entirely 表示在每一部分上。

items.example: Entireness is a rare synonym of entirety.
items.exampleCN: entireness 是 entirety 的罕见同义词。

definition_zh: 令人厌恶的；恶劣的；下流的
definition_en: very unpleasant to the senses; severe or dangerous; and morally dirty or spiteful
core_image: 一块黏糊糊的霉斑，让人下意识缩回手
scene: 厨房角落的剩菜已经长出霉点，酸味冲得人直往后退。 The milk at the back of the fridge had turned nasty.
sceneCN: 这里 nasty 是「令人厌恶的」（第 1 个义项：气味或外表使人反感）；句意为冰箱深处的牛奶已经变质发臭。图中可辨识物件：发霉的剩菜、冰箱隔层。

pos.zh: 令人厌恶的；恶劣的；下流的

derivatives.zh: 由 nasty 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「厌恶；下流」
由 nasty 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「令人厌恶地；恶意地」

senses.title: Very unpleasant to the senses
senses.titleCN: 令人厌恶的；难闻难看的
senses.definition: so unpleasant to see, smell, taste or touch that a person wants to move away from it
senses.definitionCN: 在视觉、气味、味道或触感上让人反感，使人想躲开
senses.example: A nasty smell came from the rubbish bin.
senses.exampleCN: 垃圾桶里传来一股难闻的味道。
senses.why: The earliest record of the word described something filthy, so the sense starts from physical dirt that the senses reject.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早的记录指肮脏的东西，所以词义起点是感官排斥的身体污秽。

senses.title: Severe, dangerous or hard to deal with
senses.titleCN: 恶劣的；严重的；难对付的
senses.definition: used of weather, injuries, problems or events that are severe and cause real trouble
senses.definitionCN: 用于天气、伤势、问题或事件，表示严重并带来实际麻烦
senses.example: He took a nasty fall on the icy steps.
senses.exampleCN: 他在结冰的台阶上摔了很重的一跤。
senses.why: Once the word means bad to the senses, English stretches it from what smells wrong to what goes wrong, so an injury or a storm can be nasty.
senses.whyCN: 词义从「感官上不好」扩展到「事情出岔子」，受伤或风暴这类带来麻烦的事也就成了 nasty。

senses.title: Spiteful or morally dirty
senses.definition: used of words, jokes or people that are unkind, spiteful or sexually coarse
senses.definitionCN: 用于言语、玩笑或人，表示刻薄、怀有恶意或色情粗俗
senses.example: She spread nasty rumours about her rival.
senses.exampleCN: 她散布关于对手的恶意谣言。
senses.why: Filth moves easily from the body to behaviour: a dirty mouth or a dirty trick carries the same disgust that a dirty smell does.
senses.whyCN: 「脏」很容易从身体转到行为上：一张脏嘴或一个脏手段，带来的厌恶和闻到脏东西时一样。

intro.en: The word is first recorded in Middle English as nasti, and its earlier source is disputed, so the account below marks the uncertain links.
intro.cn: 这个词最早以 nasti 的形式见于中古英语，更早的来源有争议，因此下面的叙述会标明不确定的环节。

items.en: Nasti is recorded in the fourteenth century with the sense of dirty and filthy.
items.cn: 十四世纪的文献里出现 nasti，意为肮脏的、污秽的。

items.en: One common suggestion traces it to an Old French form such as nastre, meaning filthy, but the record is thin.
items.cn: 一种常见说法把它追溯到意为「肮脏」的古法语形式 nastre，但证据很薄弱。

items.en: Another suggestion links it to Dutch nestig, literally nest-like, that is, dirty as a nest.
items.cn: 另一种说法把它联系到荷兰语 nestig，字面是「像鸟窝的」，即像窝一样脏。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the word covers not only filth but also coarse speech and spiteful behaviour.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，这个词不只指污秽，还指粗俗的言语和恶意的行为。

items.en: Modern English keeps the informal force of the word and uses it freely for bad weather, bad injuries and bad problems.
items.cn: 现代英语保留这个词的口语力度，广泛用于恶劣天气、严重伤势和棘手问题。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on the same stem; the near-meaning group collects words for disgust and unpleasantness.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词干上的形式；近义组收表示厌恶与不快之感的词。

entries.definition: The noun made from nasty with -ness, meaning the quality of being nasty.
entries.definitionCN: 由 nasty 加 -ness 构成的名词，义为「厌恶；下流」。

entries.definition: The adverb made from nasty with -ly, meaning in a nasty way.
entries.definitionCN: 由 nasty 加 -ly 构成的副词，义为「令人厌恶地；恶意地」。

entries.definition: A garden plant with bright flowers; its Latin name means nose-twister and only looks like nasty.
entries.definitionCN: 一种开亮色花的园艺植物；其拉丁名意为「扭鼻子」，只是拼写与 nasty 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: So unpleasant that it makes a person feel sick.
entries.definitionCN: 令人反胃的；极讨厌的。

entries.definition: Dirty, unpleasant and often smelling bad.
entries.definitionCN: 肮脏的；难闻的。

entries.definition: Not enjoyable or comfortable to experience.
entries.definitionCN: 令人不快的；不舒服的。

normalIntro.en: The word has a disputed stem and three productive English endings, which together cover the adjective, the noun and the adverb.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词有一个来源有争议的词干和三个能产的英语词尾，分别撑起形容词、名词和副词。

normal.en: Nasti in Middle English already meant filthy, so the disgust sense is the oldest one.
normal.cn: 中古英语里的 nasti 已经表示污秽，所以「厌恶」是最老的义项。

normal.en: Nastiness and nastily are built with plain suffixes, so the family is small and easy to keep straight.
normal.cn: nastiness 与 nastily 都由普通后缀构成，词族很小，好记不乱。

normal.en: A nasty fall and nasty weather keep the same idea: something bad has happened to you.
normal.cn: nasty fall 与 nasty weather 保留同一个想法：有坏事落到你头上。

normal.en: Nasty words are called dirty words because English reuses the language of filth for meanness.
normal.cn: 恶毒的话被叫作「脏话」，因为英语把污秽的说法挪去形容刻薄。

normal.en: The comparative is nastier, not more nasty, so the ending behaves like happy and pretty.
normal.cn: 比较级是 nastier，而不是 more nasty，词尾变化和 happy、pretty 一样。

abstract.en: A word that begins with a smell and ends with a rumour shows how one kind of disgust can spread to another.
abstract.cn: 一个词从气味开始、到谣言结束，说明一种厌恶如何蔓延到另一种。

abstract.en: Nasty is English at its most physical: the nose learns the word before the mind does.
abstract.cn: nasty 是英语里最身体化的词之一：鼻子比脑子先学会它。

abstract.en: Saying that a problem is nasty quietly admits that it may beat you.
abstract.cn: 说一个问题 nasty，其实是在悄悄承认它可能把你难倒。

examples.en: The fridge had a nasty smell after the power cut.
examples.cn: 断电之后冰箱里有一股难闻的味道。

examples.en: He took a nasty fall while running down the stairs.
examples.cn: 他跑下楼梯时重重摔了一跤。

examples.en: Her nasty remarks spoiled the whole evening.
examples.cn: 她那几句恶毒的话毁了整个晚上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「那个死地」——一提到那个地方就嫌恶地皱眉；记住 nasty 是令人厌恶的。

root: 中古英语 nasti（肮脏的、污秽的），来源不确定，一般认为与古法语 nastre 或荷兰语 nestig 有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is sensory disgust; from it the word reaches severe trouble and then dirty behaviour.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是感官上的厌恶；由此延伸到严重的麻烦，再伸向下流的行为。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sticky patch of mould that makes the hand pull back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块黏糊糊的霉斑，让人下意识缩回手。

branches.en: a bin overflowing beside a warm kitchen door
branches.cn: 温热的厨房门边堆满溢出的垃圾

branches.en: a child holding its nose at a plate of spoiled food
branches.cn: 孩子闻到变质食物时捏住鼻子

branches.en: a runner flat on the ice after a bad landing
branches.cn: 跑步的人重重摔在冰面上

branches.en: a storm tearing at the roof of a coastal house
branches.cn: 风暴撕扯海边房屋的屋顶

branches.en: a whispered rumour passing from desk to desk
branches.cn: 一句悄悄话从一张桌子传到另一张桌子

intro.en: The word has a disputed stem and three productive English endings, which build the adjective, the noun and the adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词有一个来源有争议的词干和三个能产的英语词尾，分别构成形容词、名词和副词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate has been recorded for this word; the early source itself is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录，其早期来源本身也不确定。

items.meaning: forming adjectives from nouns or stems

definition_zh: 男性的；雄性的；男子；雄性动物；阳端的
definition_en: of the sex that does not give birth; an adult man or a male animal; also the masculine or technical male side of something
core_image: 一只公鸡站在栅栏上，冠子在晨光里通红，尾羽垂下成一道弧
scene: 农场清晨，栅栏边的公鸡昂着头，羽毛在斜光里发亮。 The male bird crowed at the fence while the hens stayed in the shade.
sceneCN: 这里是「雄性的、公的」（第 2 个义项：动物中的雄性）；句意为栅栏边的公鸡打鸣时，母鸡都待在阴凉处。

derivatives.zh: 与 male 同出拉丁语 masculus，义为「有男子气质的；男性的」
由 masculine 加 -ity 构成，义为「男子气概；男性特质」
由 male 加 -ness 构成，义为「男性特质；雄性特征」

senses.title: An adult man
senses.definition: a person of the sex that does not give birth, especially an adult man
senses.definitionCN: 不生育的一性的人，尤指成年男子
senses.example: Two male nurses joined the night shift.
senses.exampleCN: 两名男护士加入了夜班。
senses.why: Latin mas named the male of any species, and English kept the noun for men while the adjective spread to animals and machines.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 mas 指任何物种中的雄性，英语保留其名词用法指男子，而形容词用法则扩展到动物与机械。

senses.title: The sex of animals and plants
senses.definition: belonging to the sex of animals or plants that produces sperm
senses.definitionCN: 属于产生精子的那一性，用于动物或植物
senses.example: The male flowers open before the female ones.
senses.exampleCN: 雄花比雌花开得早。
senses.why: Because the same biological distinction runs through plants as through animals, the word serves as a label for any organism of that sex.
senses.whyCN: 同一种生理区分在植物和动物身上一样成立，所以这个词可以用来标注任何属于那一性的生物。

senses.title: Having qualities thought typical of men
senses.titleCN: 男子气概的；男性特有的
senses.definition: having qualities that are traditionally associated with men, such as strength or a deep voice
senses.definitionCN: 具有传统上与男子相联系的特质，如力量或低沉的嗓音
senses.example: His manner was calm but unmistakably male.
senses.exampleCN: 他的举止沉静，却带着不容错认的男子气。
senses.why: A word for a biological class easily slides into a word for the behaviour expected of that class.
senses.whyCN: 一个标示生理类别的词，很容易滑向标示该类别的行为举止。

senses.title: The positive side of a connector
senses.definition: describing a plug, connector or fitting designed to enter its matching part
senses.definitionCN: 指设计成插入配对部件的插头、接头或配件
senses.example: The cable has a male plug at one end and a female one at the other.
senses.exampleCN: 这根线缆一端是阳插头，另一端是阴插头。
senses.why: Engineering borrowed the biological contrast of two mating parts and kept male for the part that fits inside.
senses.whyCN: 工程领域借用了两个配对部件的生理对立，用 male 指插进去的那一方。

intro.en: Male goes back to the Latin noun mas, whose stem mar- and diminutive masculus passed through Old French before English shortened it.
intro.cn: male 可追溯到拉丁语名词 mas，其词干 mar- 与指小形式 masculus 经古法语传入，再由英语缩略成形。

items.en: Mas meant a male person or animal, and its genitive stem was maris.
items.cn: mas 指男性的人或雄性动物，其属格词干为 maris。

items.en: Masculus was a diminutive of mas and meant male or masculine; it is the source of the English word masculine.
items.cn: masculus 是 mas 的指小形式，意为雄性的、男性的；英语 masculine 即出自它。

items.en: Old French wrote the word as masle or malle, and the l in those forms shaped the English spelling.
items.cn: 古法语把这个词写作 masle 或 malle，正是这些形式里的 l 决定了英语的拼写。

items.en: Middle English male worked as both noun and adjective, and the adjective widened from people to animals and plants.
items.cn: 中古英语的 male 兼作名词与形容词，形容词用法又从人扩展到动物与植物。

items.en: Modern English adds the technical sense of a male plug and keeps the noun for men and male animals.
items.cn: 现代英语添上「阳插头」的技术义，并保留指男子与雄性动物的名词用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same Latin stem and one misleading look-alike; the near-meaning group gathers words for men and manly character.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词干上的词与一个容易误认的形近词；近义组收指男子与男子气质的词。

entries.definition: Having qualities traditionally associated with men, from Latin masculus.
entries.definitionCN: 具有传统男性特质，源自拉丁语 masculus。

entries.definition: The quality or state of being masculine.
entries.definitionCN: 男子气概；男性特质。

entries.definition: The other biological sex; the resemblance to male is only in spelling, since it comes from Latin femella.
entries.definitionCN: 另一生理性别；只是拼写相近，词源不同，它来自拉丁语 femella。

entries.definition: Having the qualities expected of a man, built on man rather than on male.
entries.definitionCN: 具有人们期待的男子品质，由 man 而非 male 构成。

entries.definition: An adult male human being.
entries.definitionCN: 成年男性。

entries.definition: A man of good manners and social standing.
entries.definitionCN: 有礼貌、有身份的男士。

entries.definition: A boy or young man, used chiefly in British English.
entries.definitionCN: 男孩或年轻男子，主要用于英式英语。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin noun for a male, reshaped by French spelling, and its family all points back to one biological contrast.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中指雄性的名词，经法语拼写改造而定形，它的同族词都指向同一种生理对立。

normal.en: Latin mas, genitive maris, named a male, and masculus was its diminutive adjective.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mas 的属格是 maris，指雄性，而 masculus 是它的指小形容词。

normal.en: The l in male appeared in Old French forms such as masle, so the spelling changed while the meaning stayed.
normal.cn: male 里的 l 出现在 masle 这类古法语形式中，拼写变了，含义却没有变。

normal.en: Masculine and masculinity share the same Latin stem, which is why they all point back to mas.
normal.cn: masculine 与 masculinity 共用同一个拉丁词干，所以它们都回指 mas。

normal.en: Female looks like male plus fe, but it comes from Latin femella; the similarity is only in spelling, not in origin.
normal.cn: female 看起来像 male 前加 fe，其实它来自拉丁语 femella；相似只在拼写，不在词源。

normal.en: Technical writing uses male for the plug that goes inside, a direct borrowing of the biological contrast.
normal.cn: 技术写作里用 male 指插进去的那一端，这是直接借用生理上的对立。

abstract.en: A rooster on a fence post needs no adjective to announce its sex, yet English still labels it male.
abstract.cn: 站在栅栏桩上的公鸡不必用形容词宣告性别，英语仍要给它贴上 male 的标签。

abstract.en: Two identical plugs, one wider by a millimetre: the narrower one is called male because it fits in.
abstract.cn: 两个几乎一样的插头，一个宽了一毫米：较窄的那个因为插得进去而被叫作 male。

abstract.en: A deep voice and a firm handshake are read as male long before anyone checks a birth certificate.
abstract.cn: 低沉的嗓音与有力的握手，在任何人查看出生证明之前就先被读成男性。

examples.en: Two male nurses joined the night shift.
examples.cn: 两名男护士加入了夜班。

examples.en: The male flowers open before the female ones.
examples.cn: 雄花比雌花开得早。

examples.en: The cable has a male plug at one end.
examples.cn: 这根线缆一端是阳插头。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「买哦」——扛重活的多是男子，买东西的也多是他们；记住 male 是男性。

root: 拉丁语 mas（雄性，属格 maris）的指小形式 masculus 经古法语 masle 进入英语；同族词多与「男性、男子气」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the biological male sex; from there the word names an adult man, then a quality of behaviour, and finally the part of a connector that fits inside.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是生理上的雄性；词义由此指成年男子，再指一种行为气质，最后指连接件中插进去的那一端。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rooster on a fence rail, chest out, tail feathers hanging in a single curve.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只公鸡站在栅栏横木上，挺着胸，尾羽垂成一道弧。

branches.en: a man standing at the front of a crowded room
branches.cn: 站在挤满人的房间最前面的男子

branches.en: a rooster crowing before daylight
branches.cn: 天没亮就开始打鸣的公鸡

branches.en: a voice and a stride read as masculine
branches.cn: 被听成男子气概的嗓音与步态

branches.en: a plug shaped to fit only one socket
branches.cn: 只有一种插座能插进去的插头

branches.en: one word covering men and male animals
branches.cn: 同一个词同时涵盖男子与雄性动物

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin noun for a male, its diminutive adjective, the French reshaping, and English endings that name the quality.
intro.cn: 这个词依靠拉丁语中指雄性的名词、它的指小形容词、法语的改写，以及命名这种性质的英语词尾支撑。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the whole line here: mas gave masculus, and masculus reached English through French before male was shortened.
latinIntro.cn: 这里整条线索都由拉丁语提供：mas 生出 masculus，masculus 经法语进入英语，之后才缩略成 male。

items.meaning: of the sex that does not give birth

definition_zh: 使变形；使改观；转变；改造；变换
definition_en: to change the form, appearance, or nature of something completely
core_image: 毛虫变蝴蝶：还是同一个生命，模样彻底换了
scene: 旧厂房改造完工那天，居民们走进焕然一新的园区： On renovation day the designer opened the door and saw the empty shell changed into a bright library by the transform.
sceneCN: 这里 transform 是动词「使改观」（第 1 个义项：彻底改变外观或性质）；句意是旧厂房被改造成图书馆。

collocations.zh: 把 A 改造成 B

derivatives.zh: 由 transform 加 -ation 构成，义为「变形；改造；转变」
由 transform 加 -er 构成，义为「变压器；改造者」
由 transform 加 -ative 构成，义为「变革性的」

senses.title: To change the form or appearance completely
senses.definition: to change the shape or look of something entirely
senses.definitionCN: 使某物的形状或外观彻底改变
senses.example: The new paint transformed the old house.
senses.exampleCN: 新刷的漆让老房子焕然一新。
senses.why: The core image is a caterpillar becoming a butterfly: same being, new form.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是毛虫变蝴蝶：同一个生命，全新的形态。

senses.title: To change the nature or quality of something or someone
senses.definition: to change what something or someone is like in character
senses.definitionCN: 改变某物或某人的性质面貌
senses.example: Reading transformed her from a shy girl into a confident speaker.
senses.exampleCN: 阅读使她从羞涩的女孩变成自信的演讲者。
senses.why: Beyond the visible shape, the inner nature is remade.
senses.whyCN: 不止外形，内在性质也被重塑。

senses.title: To convert one form of energy or signal into another
senses.definition: to change energy or signals from one form to another
senses.definitionCN: 把能量或信号从一种形式变为另一种
senses.example: The station transforms steam power into electricity.
senses.exampleCN: 该站把蒸汽能转化为电能。
senses.why: What crosses over is form itself: energy enters one shape, leaves in another.
senses.whyCN: 跨越的正是形式本身：能量以一种形态进入，以另一种离开。

senses.title: To apply a mathematical transformation
senses.definition: to change variables or data according to a mathematical rule
senses.definitionCN: 按数学规则改变变量或数据
senses.example: The Fourier transform turns waves into frequencies.
senses.exampleCN: 傅里叶变换把波转换为频率。
senses.why: In mathematics the same object is simply re-expressed in another frame.
senses.whyCN: 数学中同一对象只是被换到另一坐标系重新表达。

intro.en: Transform comes from Latin transformare, to shape beyond or across, from trans- (across) and formare (to form), from forma, shape.
intro.cn: transform 来自拉丁语 transformare「越过原形重塑」，由 trans-（跨越）与 formare（塑形）构成，formare 出自 forma（形状）。

items.en: forma meant shape or figure, root of form.
items.cn: 拉丁语 forma 意为「形状」，是 form 的词根。

items.en: transformare meant to reshape or change the form of.
items.cn: 拉丁语 transformare 意为「重塑、改变形态」。

items.en: The word passed into French as transformer.
items.cn: 该词经法语 transformer 进入法语。

items.en: Borrowed into English with magical and physical senses.
items.cn: 进入英语时兼有魔法变身与物理改变之义。

items.en: Added senses in energy, signals, and mathematics.
items.cn: 现代英语增加能量、信号与数学的义项。

note.en: Words that look or sound close to transform, and words in the changing field.
note.cn: 与 transform 形近音近的词，以及同属改变义场的词。

entries.definition: a device that changes voltage; one who transforms
entries.definitionCN: 变压器；改造者，transform 的派生名词

entries.definition: the act or result of transforming
entries.definitionCN: 变形；改造，transform 的名词形式

entries.definition: to carry across
entries.definitionCN: 转移，与 transform 同前缀不同词根：ferre 搬运，formare 塑形

entries.definition: to make different
entries.definitionCN: 改变，最泛用的说法

entries.definition: to change into another form or use
entries.definitionCN: 转换；改装，强调用途或形式的转換

entries.definition: to improve by change
entries.definitionCN: 改革；改良，同根 formare，强调变好

entries.definition: a complete change of form
entries.definitionCN: 蜕变；变态（生物学），彻底的形态改变

definition_zh: 因此；从而；如此；这样
definition_en: as a result or consequence; in this way or manner
core_image: 断掉的桥与绕行的旧河道，两条线合成一条必经的路
scene: 暴雨把山道冲断，车队只能改走河谷里的旧路。 The mountain road was washed out; thus, the convoy took the old valley route.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（因此、所以，表结果）；句意为山道被冲毁，因此车队改走了河谷旧路。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词词尾构成的诙谐或非正式变体，义为「如此」
由本词与表示「远、至此」的词构成的固定短语，义为「到目前为止」
由本词与表示「多」的词构成的固定短语，义为「就这么多」
由本词与两个指示成分构成的固定短语，义为「如此这般」

senses.title: Introducing a result
senses.definition: used to introduce a result that follows from what was just stated
senses.definitionCN: 用来引出由前面所述自然产生的结果
senses.example: The valve was closed; thus, no steam entered the tank.
senses.exampleCN: 阀门已关闭，因此没有蒸汽进入罐体。
senses.why: The oldest sense of manner turned into a sense of consequence: the way things were left produced the next state.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的方式义转为结果义：事情被弄成那样，下一步状态便随之而来。

senses.title: In this way
senses.definition: in the manner or by the means just described
senses.definitionCN: 以刚刚描述的方式或手段
senses.example: The frame is welded thus, with one bead along each joint.
senses.exampleCN: 框架就是这样焊成的，每条接缝上走一道焊道。
senses.why: Manner is the word's original meaning, and it survives whenever the sentence describes how something is done.
senses.whyCN: 方式是这个词的本义，只要句子在描述事情怎么做，这层意思就还在。

senses.title: Up to this point
senses.definition: used in the fixed phrase thus far to mean up to the present point
senses.definitionCN: 用于固定搭配，表示到现在为止
senses.example: Thus far the trial has produced no side effects.
senses.exampleCN: 到目前为止，这次试验没有产生副作用。
senses.why: The idea of reaching a point produced a phrase for how far matters have gone.
senses.whyCN: 「到达某一点」的想法，发展出表示事情进展到何处的固定搭配。

senses.title: Therefore in academic argument
senses.definition: marking the conclusion drawn from evidence in formal prose
senses.definitionCN: 在正式文字中标示由证据推出的结论
senses.example: The data are consistent; thus the model can be accepted.
senses.exampleCN: 数据彼此一致，因此该模型可以接受。
senses.why: Research writing needs an unmistakable marker for inference, and this adverb supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 研究写作需要一个不含糊的推论标记，这个副词正好提供。

senses.title: Hence in a proof
senses.definition: introducing a step that follows necessarily from the previous line
senses.definitionCN: 引出由上一步必然得出的下一步
senses.example: Every term is divisible by three; thus the sum is divisible by three.
senses.exampleCN: 每一项都能被三整除，因此总和也能被三整除。
senses.why: Mathematics adopted the word because a proof is a chain in which each link follows from the one before.
senses.whyCN: 数学采用这个词，是因为证明就是一条每一环都由前一环导出的链。

senses.title: Accordingly in legal text
senses.definition: in statutes and contracts, marking a legal consequence that follows
senses.definitionCN: 在法规与合同中标示随之而来的法律后果
senses.example: The notice was served late and thus the claim was barred.
senses.exampleCN: 通知送达过晚，因此该项请求被排除。
senses.why: Law states cause and effect precisely, and the adverb marks the second half of that relation.
senses.whyCN: 法律要精确陈述因果，这个副词标记这一关系的后半段。

senses.title: So, in literary narration
senses.definition: in older or literary prose, describing the manner in which something was done
senses.definitionCN: 在较古旧或文学性的文字里，描述某事是怎样做成的
senses.example: He folded the letter thus and pressed the seal into the wax.
senses.exampleCN: 他就这样把信折好，把印章压进蜡里。
senses.why: Narrative keeps the manner sense alive by letting the word point at a gesture as it happens.
senses.whyCN: 叙述文字让这个词指着正在发生的动作，从而让方式义延续下来。

senses.title: So in summary
senses.definition: closing a line of argument by gathering the final point together
senses.definitionCN: 收束一段论证，把最后一点收拢起来
senses.example: Thus we may say that the two methods agree in practice.
senses.exampleCN: 由此可见，这两种方法在实际中是一致的。
senses.why: A closing word needs to sound like a conclusion drawn rather than a new claim, and this adverb does that.
senses.whyCN: 收尾的词听起来要像推出的结论而非新主张，这个副词正好如此。

intro.en: Thus is a native Old English adverb meaning in this way. It has no Latin ancestor; its earlier Germanic origin is reconstructed rather than attested.
intro.cn: 这是英语本土的古英语副词，意为「以这种方式」，没有拉丁语祖先；其更早的日耳曼语来源只有重构形式，缺乏直接文献。

items.en: Þus meant in this way and pointed at the manner of an action.
items.cn: 这个词意为「以这种方式」，指向动作的方式。

items.en: The deeper Germanic form is reconstructed from related adverbs and is not directly attested, so the earlier origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 更早的日耳曼语形式由相关副词重构而来，没有直接文献，因此更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Spelling shifted to the modern shape, and the word kept its manner sense while gaining a result sense.
items.cn: 拼写转为今天的形态，词义在保留方式义的同时发展出结果义。

items.en: Prose began to use it for consequence as well as manner; the exact date of that shift is uncertain.
items.cn: 散文开始用它兼表结果与方式；这一转变的确切年代不确定。

items.en: Mathematics, philosophy and law each adopted the adverb as a fixed sign of consequence.
items.cn: 数学、哲学与法律各自采用这个副词，作为标示结果的固定记号。

items.en: It survives mainly in formal and academic writing, while speech prefers a shorter synonym.
items.cn: 它主要存活于正式与学术写作中，口语更爱用更短的近义说法。

note.en: The first group shares a form or a letter pattern; the second group lists other connectives of consequence.
note.cn: 第一组在形态或字母组合上相近；第二组是其他表示结果的连接词。

entries.definition: A humorous or informal adverb built by adding a suffix to the word.

entries.definition: A time adverb that also begins with the same letters but marks sequence, not consequence.
entries.definitionCN: 同样以这几个字母开头的副词，但标记时间顺序而非结果。

entries.definition: A noun for a heavy dull sound, close in spelling and sound but unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 指沉闷撞击声的名词，拼写与读音都近，但并无词源关系。

entries.definition: The most explicit connective of consequence, common in formal prose.
entries.definitionCN: 最明确的结果连接词，常见于正式文字。

entries.definition: A formal connective of consequence, often followed by a noun phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 正式的结果连接词，后面常直接跟名词短语。

entries.definition: Marks a result with emphasis on the causal link.
entries.definitionCN: 标记结果，并强调因果联系。

entries.definition: Marks a result that calls for a matching response or arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 标记结果，并暗示相应采取的行动或安排。

entries.definition: The short everyday connective of result, preferred in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 最短的日常结果连接词，口语中更常用。

normalIntro.en: Thus is the little arrow in formal prose: cause first, result after it, and a manner sense underneath.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是正式文字里的小箭头：原因在前，结果在后，底下还压着一层方式义。

normal.en: Hold your hand out thus: the word can still describe the way a thing is done.
normal.cn: 把手这样伸出去：这个词至今仍能描述一件事怎么做。

normal.en: Read it as a short so: cause, semicolon, result.
normal.cn: 把它读成一个短短的「所以」：原因、分号、结果。

normal.en: Its fixed phrases are thus far and thus much.
normal.cn: 它的固定搭配是表示「至今」与「这么多」的两个短语。

normal.en: In a proof it is the arrow saying the next line must follow.
normal.cn: 在证明里，它是一支箭头，表示下一行必须跟着成立。

normal.en: It has no ending and never changes shape.
normal.cn: 它没有词尾，也从不改变形态。

abstract.en: A word that means both therefore and in this way reminds us that causes and methods are often the same thing.
abstract.cn: 一个词兼表「因此」与「如此」，提醒我们原因与方法常常是一回事。

abstract.en: Formal writing uses it to admit that a step was taken, not merely asserted.
abstract.cn: 正式写作用它来承认某一步是被走出来的，而不只是被宣称的。

abstract.en: The shorter the connective, the more it trusts the reader to follow.
abstract.cn: 连接词越短，就越相信读者能自己跟上。

examples.en: The valve was closed; thus, no steam entered the tank.
examples.cn: 阀门已关闭，因此没有蒸汽进入罐体。

examples.en: The frame is welded thus, with one bead along each joint.
examples.cn: 框架就是这样焊成的，每条接缝上走一道焊道。

examples.en: Thus we may say that the two methods agree in practice.
examples.cn: 由此可见，这两种方法在实际中是一致的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「扎斯」——「扎」住前面的原因，「斯」就是随之而来的结果：因此、如此

root: 古英语本土副词，原义为「以这种方式」，兼指方式与结果；更早的日耳曼语形式仅有重构，来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses split into the two layers the word has always had: manner in one half, consequence in the other, with fixed phrases and formal registers in between.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分成这个词自古就有的两层：一半是方式，一半是结果，中间夹着固定搭配与正式语体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a broken bridge and the old river road, two lines joined into one necessary route.
core.cn: 核心意象：断掉的桥与绕行的旧河道，两条线合成一条必经的路。

branches.en: THE RESULT: consequence is drawn both in everyday prose and in academic argument.
branches.cn: 结果：日常文字与学术论证中把结论引出。

branches.en: THE MANNER: the word shows how a thing is done, in technical or literary description.
branches.cn: 方式：在技术或文学描写中显示事情如何做成。

branches.en: THE POINT REACHED: a fixed phrase marks how far matters have gone.
branches.cn: 所到的这一步：固定搭配标示事情进展到何处。

branches.en: THE FORMAL CONSEQUENCE: a proof step or a legal effect follows of necessity.
branches.cn: 形式化的后果：证明的一步或法律效果必然随之而来。

branches.en: THE CLOSING WORD: a summary gathers its argument into one last line.
branches.cn: 收束之词：总结把论证收进最后一句。

intro.en: Thus is a native adverb with no affix of its own. The items below show its fixed phrases and the connectives it competes with.
intro.cn: 这是本族副词，本身不带词缀。下列条目展示它的固定搭配，以及与之竞争的连接词。

latinIntro.en: There are no Latin entries: the word descends from Old English and has no Latin or Greek ancestor. The list is left empty on purpose.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁词条：这个词源自古代英语，没有拉丁或希腊语祖先，清单按设计留空。

items.meaning: in this way; as a result
items.example: The word carries both manner and consequence.
items.exampleCN: 这个词同时承载方式与结果。

items.meaning: in this way, humorous or informal
items.example: The suffix adds an adverb ending to an adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾给副词再加一层副词词尾。

items.example: The phrase limits the claim to the present.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语把说法限制到眼下。

items.example: It measures the extent of what is said.
items.exampleCN: 它衡量所说内容的程度。

items.structure: English connective from a native root
items.example: It is the most explicit rival of thus.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词最明确的竞争者。

items.structure: English connective from a native root
items.example: It often leads straight into a noun phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它后面常直接接名词短语。
口语更偏爱这个短形式。

items.example: It stresses the causal link rather than the manner.
items.exampleCN: 它强调因果链，而非方式。
